title: Data from drones in Ukraine is fueling a new Wild West marketplace
content:
Data from drones in Ukraine is fueling a new Wild West marketplace
The front line is being turned into a place to train AI models, and right now it’s effectively a regulation-free zone.
Battlefields in Ukraine are littered with the remnants of drones, which are now firmly established as a critical weapon of modern warfare. But behind all that wreckage, there’s a new gold mine for the defense sector. The data drones generate will far outlast the wars in which they are used to fight, increasingly becoming part of the AI architecture that shapes even civilian life.
For every flight, unmanned systems collect thousands of points of data, from images and video to controller inputs. Together, those records show how a machine and a person responded to constantly shifting circumstances.
Ukraine has now begun converting that experience into a resource. Its Ministry of Defense announced in January that it would make millions of data points gathered during tens of thousands of drone flights available to both military contractors and commercial companies, and since then more than 100 companies and the UK government have gained access.
For a country at war, it’s a quick way to attract funding and partnerships. But this step turns the front line into an active site of model training, taking advantage of how the chaos of war creates conditions that AI companies struggle to reproduce on their own.
Other countries and battlefields are likely to follow Ukraine’s lead, but the responsibility for governing this new industry cannot fall solely on a country fighting for its survival. That legal vacuum has to be filled together by the countries and companies involved in this industry’s development.
Explosive growth
Ukraine’s battlefields are not the first to produce records used to train and develop models: American drones over Syria and Yemen collected data that informed the first generation of semiautonomous military hardware in the late 2010s.
The difference now is that access to that data is being used to develop a wider ecosystem. And the financial value to defense firms is immense: Battlefield data offers large volumes of machine experience gathered under conditions that no laboratory can produce.
That’s because the data that’s most valuable for training AI models comes from exceptions: the moment visibility disappears, a signal jams, or a human operator improvises. AI companies spend years and enormous sums trying to capture enough of these moments to make their models more robust. But war produces them at a frequency controlled testing cannot match.
This constantly changing terrain is what makes drone data valuable far beyond the battlefield. A commercial drone used for delivery or remote sensing may never encounter artillery fire, but it must still operate with incomplete information in a world where people behave unpredictably. The same problem is compressed by war into a much shorter timeline.
Processed and matched against records of what its operator was doing, that data turns operational records into training sets. Combat becomes a commercial asset.
Many conflicts have already seen this training loop happen as drone footage feeds subsequent generations of military technology, and the market is set to grow. Enabled Intelligence, an American company that specializes in processing data to become usable in AI training, says it has already made more than half a million hours of Ukrainian drone footage available to feed into the next round of models, advertising possible uses in both military and commercial systems.
Closing the data loop
Many of the drones that now define our modern age of warfare began as civilian technology. But they’ve recently been turbocharged by new, commercially available AI systems, which allow cheap machines to operate autonomously—either individually or as a flock—as the environment changes around them. Each flight then creates a record of what the system encountered.
The resulting data is critical. The controlled lab environments usually developed to train these autonomous systems can approximate failure but are no match for the live conditions of a battlefield with very real risks. Military intelligence programs have held data generated by sensor-heavy systems like Predator and Reaper drones for nearly a decade through programs like Project Maven, but access remained entirely within the defense world. The data generated was available only through restricted, classified channels for the sole purpose of developing new weapons systems that would feed back into the same military that produced the data in the first place. That experience is now being shared to a much broader development network.
The loop now closes. Commercial technologies adapted for the battlefield are generating data that can flow back into the industries from which they came, becoming part of the data infrastructure relied on by governments and the private sector alike.
Drones that were trained in the signal-jammed airspace over Ukraine are now being deployed in the agricultural sector to help farmers map and survey their fields in places lacking the cell signal necessary for previous generations of technology.
Other countries are likely to follow Ukraine in selling their battlefield data, and we are not ready for the new marketplace this will create.
Bad actors could acquire the data, but purchase controls already mitigate that risk. Intelligence operatives scrutinize potential customers’ infrastructure for ways that data could reach enemies or nefarious actors.
Training data creates a new tracing problem, though. Whereas the movement of commercial datasets can be followed when planted contact details appear two steps from the original buyer, the provenance of AI training data vanishes in a manner embedded in the technology itself. Another risk is that this use of the data creates an extractive economy in which wealthier countries far from danger benefit from the mortal threat borne by frontline states, potentially creating a market incentive for war to continue as an unending mine for digital gold.
A fraught new frontier
Existing laws regulate how militaries may conduct war. But they say almost nothing about what happens when records created in combat are stripped of their operational context, packaged as data, and licensed to companies whose products circulate far beyond where they were made.
The responsibilities of the companies that design these systems remain unsettled. Ukraine is building access controls, which are mentioned in the newly signed UK-Ukraine AI agreement, but no governments are actively working on regulating what happens when data has been absorbed into a model and crosses back into civilian markets.
Those records contain human lives. The soldiers and civilians visible in them did not agree to become training material for products that might be sold years later. But sensor data, camera footage, and coordinates from civilians fleeing a drone strike now constitute the sorts of data that inform how future machines will make decisions.
That is a problem of consent. Individuals featured in the data—be they targets, controllers, or civilians standing by—become part of the training material. The autonomous capabilities based on that data do not stop at the edge of the battlefield. Such capabilities move into other military or commercial systems like delivery vehicles or agricultural machinery. Errors and assumptions embedded in the data travel with the model even once it enters civilian life.
Battlefield data should not be treated as ordinary commercial material. But there is currently no agency or regulator that has jurisdiction over this issue. In the meantime, governments that provide access to defense data should treat it as they would a controlled weapons transfer, recording its origin, licensing its users, and restricting onward sharing. Ukraine has begun to grapple with this. Its Avengers Labs program allows companies to train models on battlefield data without giving them direct access to sensitive databases. Yet that mitigates only one part of the problem.
Governments should require disclosure when models trained on wartime material are later incorporated into civilian products. The goal of such regulation should be to make the path from combat to commerce visible.
What these companies are really mining is experience. And soldiers cannot consent to having their experience used in this way—as training data that produces model advantage and ultimately supports a product used far from where the war was fought.
The question is no longer only what the technology companies can sell for use in war. It is what they can extract from it.
To protect ourselves from the excesses of this new industry, we need a regulatory system that follows battlefield data wherever it goes, from combat to model to commercial product.
Cory Alpert is a researcher at the University of Melbourne, looking at the impact of AI on democracy. He previously served in the Biden White House.

title: Erstes Zukunftsgespräch an der HCU: Gemeinsam die Zukunft von Stadt, Bauen und Infrastruktur gestalten
content:
Erstes Zukunftsgespräch an der HCU: Gemeinsam die Zukunft von Stadt, Bauen und Infrastruktur gestalten

HCU-Präsident Prof. Dr. Jörg Müller-Lietzkow spricht über die Zukunftschancen seiner Universität

Anlässlich ihres 20-jährigen Jubiläums hat die HafenCity Universität Hamburg (HCU) am Donnerstagabend, den 04. September 2026, erstmals zu einem Zukunftsgespräch eingeladen. Vertreter:innen aus Wissenschaft, Berufspraxis, Kammern, Verwaltung und Stiftungen kamen zusammen, um über die Rolle der HCU für die Zukunft Hamburgs und die kommenden Herausforderungen des Planens, Bauens und Zusammenlebens zu diskutieren.
Im Mittelpunkt des Abends standen der Austausch über Themen des Bauens und der Stadtentwicklung sowie die Zukunftschancen der HCU.
Die Gründungsidee der HCU ist aktueller denn je
Dr. Georg Mecke, Vorsitzender des Hochschulrats der HCU, eröffnete den Abend mit einem Rückblick auf die Gründungsidee der Universität. Die Verbindung von Architektur, Bauingenieurwesen, Geomatik, Stadtplanung, Metropolenforschung und weiteren Disziplinen sei vor 20 Jahren ein mutiger Schritt gewesen – und heute aktueller denn je. „Die Zukunft des Bauens und der Stadtentwicklung entsteht nicht in einzelnen Disziplinen, sondern im Zusammenwirken“, so die zentrale Botschaft seiner Begrüßung.
Infrastruktur als Voraussetzung für gesellschaftliches Zusammenleben
Den fachlichen Impuls gab Janna Widmaier, HCU-Absolventin und Projektleiterin der Erneuerung der Eisenbahnüberführung Sternbrücke. Unter dem Titel „Die Stadt gestalten“ berichtete sie aus der Praxis eines der aktuell sichtbarsten Infrastrukturprojekte Hamburgs. Widmaier machte deutlich, dass Infrastruktur nicht nur technische Leistungsfähigkeit bedeutet, sondern eine Voraussetzung für gesellschaftliches Zusammenleben ist. Zugleich zeigte sie, wie wichtig Dialog, Transparenz und Verantwortung im Umgang mit Betroffenen, Kritik und städtischen Veränderungsprozessen sind.
Die Zukunft der HCU
HCU-Präsident Prof. Dr. Jörg Müller-Lietzkow richtete den Blick abschließend auf die kommenden Jahre. Er betonte die besondere Rolle der HCU als interdisziplinäre Universität mit starkem Praxisbezug und einem einzigartigen Standort in der HafenCity. Die HCU bilde Menschen aus, die Hamburgs Straßen, Brücken, Gebäude, Freiräume, Quartiere und Infrastrukturen künftig mitgestalten. Damit sei sie ein zentraler Ort für die Zukunftsfähigkeit der Stadt.
Verlässliche Ressourcen und starke Partnerschaften
Neben inhaltlichen Zukunftsfragen wurden auch die finanziellen Rahmenbedingungen der Universität thematisiert. Die HCU sieht sich vor der Aufgabe, Zukunftsfelder wie nachhaltiges Bauen, technische Gebäudeausrüstung, Landschaftsarchitektur, Digitalisierung, Künstliche Intelligenz und neue ingenieurwissenschaftliche Angebote weiterzuentwickeln. Dafür seien verlässliche Ressourcen und starke Partnerschaften notwendig.
Weitere Zukunftsgespräche sollen künftig den Austausch zwischen Wissenschaft und Praxis weiter stärken, um gemeinsam Impulse für die Zukunft Hamburgs zu entwickeln.
Die HafenCity Universität Hamburg (HCU)
Die HafenCity Universität Hamburg (HCU) wurde 2006 als Universität für Baukunst und Raumentwicklung gegründet. Als Technische Universität beschäftigt sie sich in Forschung und Lehre mit den zentralen Zukunftsthemen des Bauens und der Stadt. Sie erforscht das Leben und Arbeiten der Menschen in urbanen Räumen, insbesondere in Metropolregionen, mit besonderem Fokus auf den Querschnittsthemen Digitalisierung, soziale Gerechtigkeit und Klimawandel.
Ihre 45 Professorinnen und Professoren und rund 2.500 Studierenden kommen am Standort Henning-Voscherau-Platz in der namensgebenden HafenCity zusammen. Als größtes innerstädtisches Stadtentwicklungsprojekt Europas bietet die HafenCity den besonderen Reiz eines Stadtlabors vor der Haustür.

title: EDF brings €160 million, 600 MWh Navagne BESS online in Belgium - Energy Storage
content: EDF subsidiary Luminus and infrastructure fund I4B have officially commissioned a 150 MW / 600 MWh battery energy storage system in Lixhe, Belgium. Backed by a €160 million capital investment, the Navagne facility directly connects to transmission system operator Elia’s high-voltage network, establishing itself as the largest operational battery asset in the region. Sited adjacent to the existing Lixhe hydroelectric power plant, the project leverages established generation hubs and preexisting grid infrastructure to bypass interconnection bottlenecks. It reached financial close in June 2025 and was scheduled to be commissioned by October 2026. Newelec, a Luminus subsidiary, executed the medium-voltage (33 kV) distribution network build-out and retains ongoing supervision of the electrical installations.  Re-Power said on Linkedin that it performed the hot and cold commissioning. The exact battery energy storage integrator wasn’t announced, but is understood to be a Sungrow model, with 132 storage containers installed. With 600 MWh of capacity, the system’s four-hour dispatch is part of a growing trend across the Benelux region and wider. As shallow but high-value ancillary service markets come closer to saturation, developers are pivoting away from one-hour frequency response systems toward deeper energy shifting, wholesale arbitrage, and capacity provision. At €160 million for a 600 MWh system, the project-level capital expenditure lands at roughly €266.7 per kilowatt-hour. The project was realized in tandem with I4B, The Belgian Infrastructure Fund and the delivered project is its first completed investment. A video on YouTube shows more of the site . What they said: Grégoire Dallemagne, CEO of Luminus, subsidiary of EDF power solutions: “With the inauguration of this 150 MW battery storage facility, the largest in Wallonia, we are taking another important step in the energy transition. This project demonstrates how we can accelerate the development of renewable energies while strengthening grid stability. Flexibility lies at the core of our #Electrify2030 strategy. It allows us to fully embrace our role as an integrator, bridging our generation assets, storage solutions, and customer services to help users consume energy when it makes the most sense.” Mathieu Bihet, Federal Minister for Energy: “A year ago, I was here to lay the foundation stone for this project. Today, I am pleased to see this ambition has become reality. With 150 MW of power and 600 MWh of storage capacity, this battery storage facility brings new flexibility capacity to our electricity system. This is essential to strengthen the integration of renewable energies, better balance the grid, and ensure the security of our supply. I therefore welcome Luminus’s investment, which concretely contributes to building a more flexible and resilient Belgian energy system.” The post EDF brings €160 million, 600 MWh Navagne BESS online in Belgium appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: Furo and Luox Energy launch pilot for 15-minute optimization of commercial batteries - Energy Storage
content: Furo and Luox Energy will offer a combined solution for market access and optimization of commercial and industrial battery energy storage systems (BESS). The companies said they are combining Furo’s platform for battery planning, optimization and control with Luox’s time-variable electricity products. These include Luox’s “Dynamisch RLM” and “Direktvermarktung” tariffs. The aim is to optimize battery operation in every 15-minute interval. Commercial and industrial battery storage systems can perform different functions, including peak shaving, increasing self-consumption, shifting electricity consumption and feed-in, or providing marketable flexibility. The most appropriate operating strategy depends on the individual site, load profile, generation assets and battery configuration. The companies also need to determine which application should take priority. Furo’s platform covers the entire battery storage lifecycle, from system design through to forecast-based operation. For the latter, Furo forecasts peak loads, generation and electricity prices and operates the battery accordingly, either through its own energy management system or on top of an existing energy management system. Luox Energy will provide market access under the cooperation. “LUOX Dynamisch RLM” links electricity procurement for commercial and industrial customers to 15-minute wholesale electricity prices, the companies said. This allows periods of low electricity prices to be used for battery charging. The “LUOX Direktvermarktung” tariff covers electricity fed into the grid. Electricity fed into the grid is also marketed based on 15-minute wholesale prices. For suitable systems, this means that electricity procurement, as well as the marketing and timing of electricity feed-in, can be incorporated into the economic assessment. Furo’s optimization determines when electricity is fed into the grid based on forecasts for prices, generation and load. The cooperation will begin with selected pilot projects. The companies will test how the battery systems operate under Furo’s optimization in real-world conditions. They will assess how operating schedules can be adapted to the 15-minute prices of Luox’s products, including how peak shaving, self-consumption and market optimization can be balanced in day-to-day operation and what revenue the marketing of available capacity can generate. The companies said the findings will be incorporated into the development of additional battery storage projects. They also plan to launch joint sales, communications and information initiatives. Christian Chudoba, managing director of Lumenaza, said commercial battery storage should be planned and operated by considering on-site energy management, grid electricity procurement and electricity feed-in together. He said the partnership with Furo would allow operators to factor market access into project planning from an early stage and improve the economics of solar-plus-storage systems. title: Norvento expands into utility-scale energy storage in Latin America - Energy Storage
content: Spanish renewable energy company Norvento Enerxía is expanding its focus in Latin America’s growing energy storage market, with Brazil, Chile, Argentina, Mexico and Guatemala among its priority markets. The company plans to supply its new nXL power conversion technology to utility-scale storage projects while building on existing experience in microgrids and industrial self-consumption. Norvento Enerxía, a renewable energy company based in Lugo, Galicia, Spain, wants to expand its presence in Latin America as energy storage deployment accelerates across the region. Founded as an engineering company and later expanding into wind and hydropower project development, Norvento added an industrial division in 2009 focused on manufacturing proprietary technology, mainly wind turbines and power electronics equipment. Lucas López Piñeiro, Norvento’s business development manager, told pv magazine that the company already has experience in Latin America, although its activity to date has focused mainly on microgrids, industrial self-consumption and smaller-scale energy storage systems. In Argentina, Norvento has worked with local partners for several years and has supplied equipment for commercial and industrial projects, López Piñeiro said. The company has also participated in projects in the Caribbean, particularly in the Dominican Republic, where he sees opportunities linked to energy security and the increasing deployment of solar power. Many of these projects have used Norvento’s nGM converter family, with power ratings of between 50 kW and 200 kW. The equipment is designed for energy storage and microgrid applications, including off-grid systems combining PV, small wind turbines, conventional generation and batteries. López Piñeiro said Norvento’s strength in the commercial and industrial segment is providing solutions for such microgrids. Strategy for Latin America Norvento’s new strategy in Latin America has a different scale. A key objective of its recent participation in Intersolar South America was to present the nXL family, designed for large-scale energy storage and solar generation projects. López Piñeiro said Norvento does not necessarily intend to act as a full BESS integrator in the utility-scale segment. Instead, it will primarily supply power electronics to system integrators, battery manufacturers and developers capable of integrating complete systems. This approach reflects the economics of energy storage projects, he said. Batteries account for around 70% to 75% of total system costs, while power electronics represent a substantially smaller share. As a result, full BESS integration and system-wide warranties are generally handled by the integrator or battery supplier. nXL converters The new nXL reaches up to 9 MVA per unit and is designed for large-scale energy storage installations. Norvento highlights its modular architecture, efficiency of close to 99% and advanced grid-support capabilities. These include grid-forming and grid-following functions, voltage and frequency regulation, black start, STATCOM and active filtering. López Piñeiro expects these capabilities to become increasingly important as Latin American power systems integrate larger volumes of solar and wind generation. Norvento also sees potential advantages in the equipment’s thermal design for several markets in the region. The nXL has a fully sealed IP65 enclosure and combines liquid cooling with HVAC. According to López Piñeiro, this configuration allows the equipment to maintain its rated power at temperatures of up to 40 C while reducing maintenance requirements associated with air filters. The company believes these characteristics could be particularly suitable for arid locations and areas exposed to high levels of dust, humidity or demanding temperatures, including parts of Chile, Argentina and Brazil. Norvento’s international expansion in power technology is also coinciding with the development of a new factory in Lugo. The company is finalizing neFO, Norvento Enerxía Factory Zero, a facility of approximately 23,000 square meters dedicated to manufacturing power electronics equipment. The project received €27.5 million ($32 million) from the European Commission’s Innovation Fund. López Piñeiro said the facility will have potential manufacturing capacity of up to 16 GW and will support Norvento’s industrialization process and the launch of its nXL product range. Countries in focus Norvento is not concentrating its Latin American strategy on a single country. López Piñeiro identified Brazil, Chile and Argentina, along with Mexico and Guatemala, as the company’s current focus markets. Peru and Colombia are also on its radar, although they are not currently among its priority markets. He considers Chile one of the clearest examples of how the region’s storage market could evolve. Strong growth in solar and wind generation, combined with transmission constraints and curtailment, has accelerated the deployment of energy storage. López Piñeiro said similar dynamics are beginning to emerge in other countries. He argued that having generation capacity alone is not enough, as power must also be available when it is needed. He sees Argentina, Mexico and Guatemala incorporating storage into new procurement mechanisms in an effort to avoid some of the problems encountered by markets after deploying large volumes of renewable generation. Brazil could play a particularly important role in this development. Norvento is monitoring the evolution of capacity procurement mechanisms and potential local-content requirements. López Piñeiro said the company is assessing how it could adapt if such requirements eventually affect the participation of foreign suppliers. For now, however, Norvento has not announced plans for an industrial presence in Brazil. Beyond the regulatory differences between individual markets, López Piñeiro identified a common factor across much of the region: growing solar and wind capacity is increasing the need for resources that can provide flexibility and firm power to electricity systems. He said energy storage is the key tool available to renewable generation for providing this firmness. In his view, growth in Brazil could also have a knock-on effect across Latin America by attracting integrators, manufacturers and developers to the region. Norvento wants to be present wherever integrators and developers capable of integrating storage are building projects, López Piñeiro said. The company sees Chile as evidence of the potential for the market and expects Brazil to help accelerate the development of energy storage across Latin America. title: Horizonte Group, Metelligent and Einklang target battery storage for C&I customers - Energy Storage
content: Lucerne, Switzerland-based Horizonte Group AG is developing a joint battery storage service with its subsidiaries Horizonte-Group Technik (HGT), based in Cologne, and Metelligent, a joint venture with German energy supplier EAM. Cologne-based energy supplier Einklang NE Solutions, also known as Einklang Energy, is the third partner. The companies aim to provide a joint implementation service for manufacturing companies, logistics operators and retailers with annual electricity consumption of around 250 MWh or more that want to optimize battery storage under Germany’s planned Market Integration of Storage and Charging Points (MiSpeL) rules. HGT will handle installation, project planning and registration of metering concepts, while Metelligent will install meters for registered power metering (RLM). Einklang will be responsible for operating, optimizing and marketing the battery systems. The partners are targeting 50 joint projects in the first year. A competitive metering point operator will be responsible for metering point operations in each project. Germany’s Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) published an updated working version of its MiSpeL rules in early August. The rules are scheduled to take effect on Oct. 1, subject to transitional periods. The partnership is targeting a market expected to emerge from a provision known as the separation option. It would allow battery storage systems to charge from both photovoltaic installations and the grid without affecting the PV system’s eligibility for support. The companies said this configuration must be implemented from the outset. “Anyone who only adds the metering concept later is giving up the benefits of the separation option,” said Marko Dreskrüger, managing director of HGT. The main bottleneck for such projects is the metering concept, which requires electricity volumes to be allocated at 15-minute intervals according to specified calculation formulas. This requires RLM meters at different metering points and must be incorporated into project planning from the beginning. The partners expect their joint approach to reduce project timelines by improving coordination between different trades. MiSpeL is also expected to significantly change the economics of battery storage projects. “A battery that only cuts peak loads uses a fraction of its potential,” said Lucas Jonas, CEO of Einklang. “From October, it can trade, and that means operations management will determine what a project ultimately earns.” The companies said similar projects have often stalled because of regulatory uncertainty. They now expect demand to increase significantly, with the first joint projects already in preparation. title: AES Andes begins testing 340 MW/1,360 MWh BESS in Chile - Energy Storage
content: AES Andes has begun testing the battery energy storage system (BESS) at its Cristales project in Chile’s Antofagasta region. The BESS has a power output of 340 MW and four hours of duration, equivalent to 1,360 MWh of storage capacity. The company is using the testing phase to verify the performance of the equipment, control systems and safety devices. AES Andes said it will also begin commissioning the solar plant at the complex soon. In its latest corporate information, the company puts Cristales’ solar capacity at 287 MW to 288 MW, while Chile’s Ministry of Energy lists the project as having 400 MW of PV capacity in testing. The ministry’s latest Energy Sector Construction and Investment Projects Report, published in July, already listed the Cristales BESS among systems undergoing testing. At 340 MW/1,360 MWh, it was the second-largest system in the portfolio by power output, behind Grenergy’s 430 MW/3,010 MWh Elena Phase I BESS. The project has undergone several configuration changes since it was originally proposed. When submitted for environmental assessment in 2023, it comprised 379 MW of PV and a BESS of up to 542 MW with five hours of duration. Cristales received environmental approval in April 2024. The approved configuration included up to 340 MW of solar and 542 MW of storage with five hours of duration, as well as the Cristales substation and a 220 kV transmission line. The planned investment was then $710 million. In August 2025, AES Andes announced the start of construction of Cristales and the Pampas project. For Cristales, the company then reported a configuration of 288 MW of solar and 340 MW of storage. The two projects represented a combined investment of more than $1.1 billion. title: Optimizing PV-driven heat pump operation for homes with poor thermal insulation - pv magazine Global
content:
A research group in China has proposed a near-zero-energy retrofit strategy for traditional dwellings on the western Sichuan Plateau, combining rooftop PV with an air-source heat pump.
The researchers said the region’s high altitude, low ambient temperatures and strong solar radiation make it suitable for the approach, while its traditional homes typically suffer from high energy consumption and inadequate thermal comfort during the winter heating season.
“These buildings embody historical and cultural values and constitute an important component of rural architectural heritage,” the scientists said. “Most of these dwellings adopt stone–wood structural systems with thick walls but insufficient thermal insulation performance, resulting in poor indoor thermal environments during winter. Heating is generally provided by burning firewood or coal, which not only exhibits low energy efficiency but also causes air pollution and ecological pressure.”
The researchers selected a traditional dwelling in Zhibo Village, Maerkang, as a case-study building. The three-story stone-and-wood house has a total floor area of approximately 399 m², a height of 9.6 meters, 400-mm-thick walls and a slate-covered roof. Its window-to-wall ratio is 11% on the southern facade and 8% on the western facade.
Maerkang has a high-altitude continental monsoon climate, with long, cold winters and more than 120 frost days per year. Average January temperatures range from -6 C to -3 C, while nighttime temperatures can fall below -10 C. The area receives more than 2,000 hours of sunshine and approximately 3,700 MJ/m² of solar radiation per year.
The researchers recreated the case-study building in AutoCAD and SketchUp before importing the 3D model into Sware to simulate its indoor thermal environment and heating demand. They set the indoor target temperature at 16 C during the heating season and the ventilation rate at 0.5 air changes per hour. They then conducted hourly simulations to calculate annual energy consumption and winter heating loads.
The scientists converted the calculated heating load into the electricity required by a wall-mounted, low-temperature air-source heat pump. They assumed a seasonal coefficient of performance (COP) of 2.54, with the heat pump capable of supplying water at temperatures above 45 C when the ambient temperature is -15 C.
They then entered the calculated electricity demand into PVsyst to optimize the PV array’s orientation, tilt angle and size. The proposed system features 61 m² of 745 W heterojunction (HJT) bifacial, double-glass solar modules.
The simulations showed total heating demand of 15,670.9 kWh over the winter heating season, corresponding to electricity consumption of 6,162.2 kWh for the heat pump.
The researchers found that a 40-degree tilt angle was optimal for achieving zero-energy heating. They determined that the optimal rooftop PV installation area was 61 m², equivalent to 15.2% of the building’s total roof area. “By utilizing 210 mm heterojunction (HJT) bifacial double-glass modules with a conversion efficiency of up to 24%, an installation area of only 61 m
is required. This accounts for just 95.2% of the total available roof area, demonstrating that near-zero energy operation can be achieved without excessive modification to the traditional building envelope,” they emphasized.
“The total cost of the proposed system (including modules and installation) is approximately CNY 29,800 ($4,437), which represents only 19.2% of the local rural household’s annual disposable income,” the researchers added. “With an investment payback period of approximately 14 years (based on local electricity prices of CNY 0.52/kWh and annual savings of CNY 3,624), the scheme proves to be financially accessible for residents.”
The article “
Innovative photovoltaic heating for ethnic traditional dwellings towards near-zero energy heating on Tibetan plateau
” was presented in
Case Studies in Thermal Engineering
Researchers from China’s Southwest Minzu University,
Sichuan University
Tongji University
have participated in the research. “The results of this study provide useful methodological guidance and preliminary design references for the promotion of near-zero energy heating in similar rural contexts, while acknowledging that site-specific adjustments and further validation are necessary before broad application,” the academics concluded.

title: France updates list of certified low-carbon photovoltaic modules - pv magazine Global
content:
Certisolis
, a French certification body specializing in PV products and systems, has updated its
list of modules that have obtained a Simplified Carbon Assessment
(Évaluation Carbone Simplifiée, ECS). These certificates demonstrate compliance with the carbon-footprint criteria required to qualify for certain French support mechanisms, notably the S21 feed-in tariff and tenders organized by the French Energy Regulatory Commission (CRE).
The updated list provides information on valid ECS certificates, including the relevant module references, manufacturers, technologies, maximum power ratings, and the carbon-footprint thresholds they meet.
To facilitate the transition between the previous and new certification systems, Certisolis has also launched an online calculator. The tool allows users to convert the carbon value of an existing PPE2 certificate, issued under France’s second Multiannual Energy Program (PPE), into a new value designated as “non-LCA,” referring to a calculation that does not use the previous life-cycle assessment (LCA) methodology.
This new method is specifically required for the new CRE PPE2 tenders for building-mounted PV projects. Rather than analyzing the carbon impact of each stage of the module manufacturing process, as under the previous methodology, it uses an overall score based on the countries in which production takes place.
Before production begins, manufacturers can also request a provisional, or temporary, ECS certificate. This allows them to market a “low-carbon” version of a module and bid for future projects before purchasing all the components required to manufacture it.
“Some module manufacturers wait until they have ‘firm’ orders for low-carbon modules—which qualify for the S21 tariff—before sourcing ‘low-carbon’ components, which are more expensive,” Certisolis notes in a publication on the subject.
Once a sale of low-carbon modules intended to qualify for the S21 tariff has been finalized, for example, the manufacturer must purchase the low-carbon components specified in the temporary certificate.
The temporary certificate, however, cannot be used for commissioning. The modules purchased and installed must correspond exactly to the part numbers and components specified in the final certificate. Their manufacturing date must also fall within the certificate’s validity period.

title: Vertical rooftop PV arrives in Ireland - pv magazine Global
content:
Vertical solar specialist Over Easy Solar has installed its first vertical PV system in Ireland.
Located in Dublin, the 5.37 kW system features 21 of Over Easy Solar’s VPV Units comprised of the company’s third-generation XM-3 QUATTRO-256S, a preassembled, lightweight vertical bifacial photovoltaic unit.
The installation was installed directly on a green roof through Over Easy Solar’s ongoing partnership with Sempergreen, a Dutch company specializing in sustainable urban nature solutions.
Keelin Currivan, International Customer Solutions Advisor at Over Easy Solar, told
pv magazine
such installations prove that customers do not have to choose between having a green roof and a rooftop solar installation.
“The panels manage rainwater and provide thermal regulation for the roof, while the vegetation boosts panel output via the albedo effect without shading the plants themselves,” Currivan explained. “It’s a genuine case for combining biodiversity and clean energy generation on commercial rooftops, rather than treating them as competing uses of the same space.”
The installation was carried out by Irish renewable energy and electrical contractor company Solar Precision. In a statement to
pv magazine
, the company explained it chose to utilize Sempergreen’s green roof system with the Over Easy Solar’s vertical PV system “because it offered an innovative way to maximize renewable energy generation while preserving the environmental and biodiversity benefits of a green roof.”
“The system aligns with our commitment to delivering sustainable solar solutions and gave us the opportunity to be the first solar PV company in Ireland to install this technology as a case study,” the company’s statement continues.
Solar Precision added that since completion, the project has demonstrated that vertical solar panels can be successfully integrated with a green roof without compromising performance or maintenance.
“As an early adopter of this system in Ireland, we’ve gained valuable knowledge and confidence in the technology, and we’re excited about the opportunities it creates for future commercial and residential green roof projects,” the company said.
Over Easy Solar’s latest expansion follows its
first installation in the US
earlier this year with a 100 kW vertical PV system in New York. Since then, the company also installed its first system in
Vancouver, Canada
In April, Over Easy Solar shared that its vertical bifacial PV system had
outperformed
a conventionally-tilted monofacial rooftop PV system in the UK across all seasons during a year-long study.

title: Australia continues heavy investment in solar research - pv magazine Global
content:
Researchers from
University of New South Wales
(UNSW), have been awarded the bulk of a AUD 105.6 million ($76.0 million) investment for ultra low-cost solar research from the
Australian Renewable Energy Agency
(ARENA) for 12 separate solar projects.
In total, the AUD 64.8 million allocation is the university’s largest single investment in solar photovoltaic research.
UNSW Deputy Vice-Chancellor Research and Enterprise Professor Bronwyn Fox said ever since UNSW’s pioneering work developing high-efficiency silicon solar cells 50 years ago, the university has been a leader in solar energy research.
“UNSW is thrilled to partner with ARENA on these 12 projects which continue to build on this strength and help drive the development of more affordable solar technology,” Fox said.
Eleven of the projects are attached to the UNSW’s School of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering, and one from the School of Chemistry.
The successful projects are:
Lower-temperature connections for advanced solar panels
Awardee: Professor
Brett Hallam
Grant: AUD 5.4 million
This project aims to make solar panels more sustainable by reducing the amount of bismuth and silver used in their manufacture, as well as lowering the temperatures needed to produce them.
Making silicon solar panels more efficient and durable
Awardee: Professor Timothy Schmidt
Grant: AUD 7.1 million
UNSW and its partners will develop two technologies to improve silicon solar panels. One will convert ultraviolet (UV) light, while the other will help protect solar cells from damage caused by UV exposure.
Testing next-generation solar panels in real-world conditions
Awardee: Dr Jessica Yajie Jiang
Grant: AUD 5.6 million
UNSW will field-test perovskite and tandem solar modules from different manufacturers in outdoor conditions. The project will also use laboratory and accelerated testing to track how the panels perform, understand why they degrade and compare real-world results with laboratory findings.
Improving solar panel durability in Australian conditions
Awardee: Professor
Bram Hoex
Grant: AUD 6.5 million
UNSW and its partners will develop a framework to test and validate the reliability of solar panels. The project will combine laboratory testing, outdoor trials in different Australian climates, advanced diagnostics and modelling to understand how and why panels degrade, and how long they are likely to last.
Making perovskite-silicon solar panels more efficient and reliable
Awardee: Scientia Professor Xiaojing Hao
Grant: AUD 6.3 million
UNSW and its partners will develop and test solar cells and panels that combine perovskite and silicon. Using UNSW’s technology, the two parts can be made separately before being joined together. The project will improve the materials and manufacturing processes, test how reliably the panels perform in the laboratory and outdoors, and trial larger-scale production with industry partners.
Using AI and advanced manufacturing to improve tandem solar panels
Awardee: Professor Ziv Hameiri
Grant: AUD 5.1 million
This project will help develop larger tandem solar panels that convert more than 30 per cent of sunlight into electricity. It will use machine learning and advanced manufacturing technologies to improve reliability, lower production costs, detect problems earlier and help manufacturers optimise the production process.
Developing more efficient and affordable tandem solar cells
Awardee: Dr Kaiwen Sun
Grant: AUD 6.3 million
UNSW is developing solar cells that combine chalcogenide and silicon materials. The project aims to improve efficiency, reduce costs and help create next-generation solar panels that convert up to 30 per cent of sunlight into electricity.
Using AI to discover new solar materials
Awardee: Dr Ning Song
Grant: AUD 5.2 million
UNSW will use AI and modelling to find new solar materials for next-generation silicon tandem solar cells. The project aims to support solar modules that can reach 30 per cent efficiency by using an AI-enabled discovery platform.
Developing new materials to make silicon solar cells more efficient
Awardee: Associate Professor Murad Jehangir Yusuf Tayebjee
Grant: AUD 5.1 million
This project will develop new organic layers to improve the efficiency of silicon solar cells and reduce manufacturing costs. The materials will be compatible with existing production methods, making it easier for manufacturers to adopt the technology. The project could support future commercialisation through licensing, material supply and partnerships with solar manufacturers.
Designing solar panels for specific sites to reduce costs
Awardee: Professor Brett Hallam
Grant: AUD 4.4 million
UNSW will design solar panels tailored to the conditions of individual solar farms. The project aims to improve performance and increase the value of large-scale solar projects while reducing the cost of generating electricity.
Using AI to improve solar farm operations
Awardee: Professor Ziv Hameiri
Grant: AUD 4.7 million
This project will develop a digital platform to help solar farms predict faults, manage risks and reduce operating costs. It will support more efficient maintenance and help build Australian expertise in using artificial intelligence and machine learning to manage large-scale solar farms.
Using daylight imaging to detect solar panel problems
Awardee: Professor Thorsten Trupke
Grant: AUD 3.1 million
This project will develop faster ways to use daylight imaging to assess the quality and condition of solar panels. The technology could help operators detect defects caused during manufacturing or transport, support warranty claims and make better maintenance decisions.
UNSW Dean of Engineering Professor Julien Epps said the funding enables some of the leading experts worldwide in solar photovoltaics to work hand-in-hand with industry to drive forward innovative research and development that is pivotal to the energy transition and pivotal to climate change mitigation.

title: Multi-source heat pump test bench explores coupling with solar, thermal storage - pv magazine Global
content:
Chinese educational and research laboratory equipment manufacturer Micronewton Technology Development has delivered a multi-source energy laboratory system to an undisclosed research institution in China. The system is designed for university-level teaching and research into heat pumps, solar energy and thermal storage.
At the center of the installation is the company’s R306 Water-to-Air Heat Exchangers Apparatus, an experimental heat pump platform that allows users to switch between air-source, water-source and simulated ground-source operating conditions on a single test bench.
The system operates on a vapor-compression refrigeration cycle and uses 1,1,1,2-tetrafluoroethane (R134a) as the refrigerant. Its compressor has a rated power of 276 W, while the system has a stated cooling capacity of 304.8 W.
The test bench incorporates a fin-and-tube evaporator for air-source operation, a plate heat exchanger for water-source operation and a soil-source simulation unit with adjustable electric heating.
The water-source simulator features an adjustable heater rated from 0 W to 2,000 W, while the soil-source simulator has an adjustable capacity of up to 1,200 W. These components allow researchers to vary source-side temperatures and evaluate their effects on heat pump performance.
The platform measures refrigerant pressure, temperature and flow, as well as water temperature, water flow and compressor electricity consumption. According to the manufacturer, the measurements can be used to determine the heating coefficient of performance (COP), analyze compression ratios and compare heat pump performance at different evaporation and condensation temperatures.
The R306 system has a condensing heat-transfer area of 0.47 m². The source-side heat-transfer areas are 4.5 m² for air, 0.47 m² for water and 1.8 m² for the simulated ground source. The maximum stated outlet water temperature is 75 C.
The equipment is intended primarily for university teaching and energy research rather than commercial building heating. The broader laboratory installation, however, extends beyond the heat-pump test bench. MicroNewton said it combines solar panels, phase-change thermal storage, insulated hot-water storage, additional heat exchangers, circulation pumps and a centralized data-acquisition and control system.
The configuration allows researchers to investigate interactions between solar generation, heat pumps, thermal storage and energy demand. Experiments can include solar-assisted heat pump heating and the coordinated operation of heat pumps and thermal storage.

title: Study reveals high-altitude limitations in solar irradiance models - pv magazine Global
content:
Researchers have assessed the reliability of models used to estimate direct and diffuse irradiance from global horizontal irradiance (GHI) data at two sites in southern Peru. The study identifies a systematic, altitude-dependent divergence between the model results and
Solargis
satellite data, with potential implications for estimating photovoltaic (PV) yields in Andean regions.
The study, “
GHI-based PV yield assessment in high-altitude Andean sites: workflow performance and systematic limitations of irradiance decomposition models
,” compares two sites with contrasting climates: Cota Cota, located 4,240 meters above sea level on the Peruvian Altiplano, and Pampas de Majes, at 1,498 meters above sea level in an arid coastal valley in southern Peru.
The researchers used GHI and ambient temperature measurements recorded between 2021 and 2023. They used the data to adapt ERA5 meteorological reanalysis data with multilayer perceptron models, a type of neural network, to reconstruct a 25-year hourly climatology for the 2000-24 period.
Based on these time series, they generated representative meteorological years and estimated diffuse horizontal irradiance (DHI) and direct normal irradiance (DNI).
For the irradiance decomposition, the researchers used the Engerer2 model with two clear-sky schemes. The first was Threlkeld-Jordan, which was used in the original calibration of the Engerer2 model. The second was ARGPv2, an empirical model developed specifically for high-altitude sites in the Andes of northwestern Argentina, in the provinces of Salta and Jujuy, and recalibrated using the McClear clear-sky model.
Engerer2 is an empirical decomposition model that separates GHI into its direct and diffuse components. It uses a clear-sky model as a reference to describe expected irradiance under cloud-free conditions. Threlkeld-Jordan and ARGPv2 provide this clear-sky reference, with ARGPv2 designed to better represent the atmospheric conditions found at high-altitude Andean sites.
The researchers then fed the resulting irradiance components into a Liu-Jordan transposition model to calculate irradiance on the plane of the PV modules. This model is a widely used solar-energy model for estimating how much solar irradiance reaches a tilted surface, such as a PV module, from irradiance measured or estimated on a horizontal surface.
They subsequently applied a PV production model based on standard test conditions (STC) to calculate annual generation across a full matrix of module tilt and orientation combinations.
The procedure allowed the researchers to assess how differences introduced during irradiance decomposition ultimately affect energy yield estimates for PV installations.
The limited availability of direct DNI and DHI measurements is one of the main challenges facing solar resource assessments in many parts of the Andes. Where only GHI measurements are available, both components must be estimated using models, introducing an additional source of uncertainty.
Differences with Solargis
Because direct DNI and DHI measurements were unavailable at the two study sites, the researchers compared their decomposition results with Solargis data, an independent dataset based on satellite observations and atmospheric models.
The comparison revealed a systematic divergence between the two approaches that, according to the researchers, varies with altitude.
The finding is particularly relevant to PV projects on the Altiplano and in other high-altitude areas of the Andes, where atmospheric conditions differ from those at the locations used to calibrate many conventional irradiance decomposition models.
The study highlights a limitation of solar resource assessment methods based exclusively on GHI. Although these approaches can reconstruct long-term time series and estimate PV production at sites without comprehensive solar radiation measurements, uncertainty associated with separating direct and diffuse irradiance can become systematic at high altitudes.
The researchers said the findings also point to the need for local validation of models used in PV resource and yield assessments in the Andes, particularly when the results are used for project sizing or long-term generation forecasts.

title: Delayed inverter startup can reduce a solar plant’s annual energy yield by 1.88%. - pv magazine Global
content:
Brazilian researchers have found that delayed photovoltaic inverter startup can result in annual energy losses of 1.88% at a utility-scale solar plant. They analyzed 2023 operational data from a PV plant in the western part of the Brazilian state of São Paulo and developed a methodology to quantify losses associated with delayed inverter startup after sunrise.
The scientists said inverter startup can be delayed even when irradiance levels are sufficient for power generation. At the plant analyzed, they recorded delays of up to four hours after sunrise.
The proposed methodology primarily relies on sunrise times and the plant’s alternating-current (AC) active power data. Plane-of-array (POA) irradiance measurements are required only during the configuration and validation stages, reducing the instrumentation needed for the analysis.
Fluxograma da estrutura proposta. | Imagem: Laboratório de Energia e Sistemas Fotovoltaicos Marcelo Villalva (LESF-MV) da Unicamp.
Losses after sunrise
The results showed that more than 55% of annual losses associated with inverter startup delays occurred within the first 90 minutes after sunrise. The researchers also found that losses varied throughout the year.
A quarterly analysis showed that the first half of the year, corresponding to summer and autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, accounted for 68.8% of the recorded losses. The researchers said the results indicate that assessing inverter behavior at the beginning of the daily generation period could help identify opportunities to improve plant performance.
The study also revealed significant differences among the eight inverters analyzed. Monthly losses associated with startup delays ranged from 0.14% to 5.02% of each inverter’s energy generation.
According to the researchers, the variability indicates that startup delays do not necessarily affect all inverters at a plant equally. Identifying the units responsible for the largest losses could therefore enable more targeted operational interventions.
Performance assessment
The researchers said losses caused by inverter startup delays can be difficult to distinguish from other sources of performance losses at PV plants. Their methodology uses sunrise as a reference point to determine when inverters should begin operating and compares the expected startup behavior with recorded power output.
The approach makes it possible to distinguish startup losses from other factors affecting energy generation, including system unavailability, component mismatch, and weather conditions.
At the plant analyzed, inverter startup delays resulted in annual energy losses equivalent to 1.88% of total generation. The researchers said the figure is comparable to losses typically considered in PV system performance and availability assessments.
They said the methodology can be applied to utility-scale PV plants using existing operational data, helping operators identify inverter startup issues and improve plant performance.
Researchers from the Marcelo Villalva Photovoltaic Energy and Systems Laboratory (LESF-MV) at the University of Campinas (Unicamp) conducted the study. The research team included João Frederico Souza de Paula, Marcel Veloso Campos, João Lucas de Souza Silva, Marcelo Vinícius de Paula, Valentin Ferrer, Gustavo Fraidenraich, and Tárcio André dos Santos Barros.
The study, “
A method for quantifying availability losses caused by PV inverter start-up delays in a large-scale PV power plant: A case study in Southeastern Brazil
,” was published in
Electric Power Systems Research

title: Alight switches on 101 MW solar project in Finland - pv magazine Global
content:
Nordic solar developer Alight and automotive safety supplier Autoliv have inaugurated the 101 MW Eurajoki solar park.
Located on Finland’s west coast, the park is built, owned and operated by Alight. It will generate around 100 GWh annually, equivalent to the consumption of approximately 20,000 households, making it one of the largest in the country.
The electricity generated by the plant will be delivered to Autoliv under a long-term virtual power purchase agreement (PPA) first signed in
April 2025
, billed as the largest in Finland’s history at the time.
A statement published by Alight explains that long-term corporate PPAs are becoming an increasingly common route for businesses to secure predictable energy costs, with this agreement part of a broader, global climate strategy across Autoliv’s operations.
The solar park is made up of two distinct sites brought together by a shared substation. Alight says the two-site design allowed the project’s environmental protection measures to be tailored to local conditions at each location, with one site’s biodiversity plan including habitat restoration and improved wetland edges, and the other featuring a new pond.
The project was backed by €46 million ($53.5 million) of senior debt from banks ABN AMRO and SEB.
Alexander Rudberg, Alight’s Head of Development, told
pv magazine
the company is planning to add a co-located battery storage to the Eurajoki solar park.
“The current plan is for a 30 MW/60 MWh battery system to be in place in 2027,” he confirmed.
Rudberg added that in the Finnish region of Satakunta, where the Eurajoki project is located, Alight has a further four projects under development totaling 360 MW of solar and 150 MW of battery energy storage.
“They are in various stages of development, for example one has a grid connection agreement signed and two have received approved permits,” he shared.
Additional figures from Alight put its total solar and storage pipeline across Finland at in excess of 1 GW.
Finland installed
of utility-scale solar during the first half of 2026, taking cumulative utility-scale capacity to 842 MW. The commissioning of the Eurajoki project brings the country closer to 1 GW of large-scale solar.
Finland’s largest operational solar project is the 204 MW Kalanti solar park, which came online earlier this year.

title: Global polysilicon market stagnates as China price rally struggles for traction - pv magazine Global
content:
The Global Polysilicon Marker (GPM), the OPIS benchmark for polysilicon produced outside China, was assessed at $19.227/kg, or $0.040/W, unchanged from the previous week, according to the OPIS Global Solar Markets Report released on Sept. 1.
Global polysilicon market participants said the market is currently in a state of temporary stagnation, particularly reflected in reduced transaction activity.
A source at a major integrated manufacturer said global polysilicon demand is currently very weak, partly due to competition from compliant, traceable Chinese polysilicon under the U.S. Section 232 framework. The source said global prices cannot realistically fall to the $7/kg level of Chinese traceable material, adding that buyers have little reason to pay close to global producers’ costs when compliant Chinese material is available far cheaper.
Another market participant agreed, noting that even when suppliers indicate that prices are “negotiable,” buyers still lack sufficient demand. Price stability will depend largely on how strictly U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) scrutinizes the supply chains of imported products, the source said.
Reports of heightened U.S. customs scrutiny have continued to emerge. A White House report released in late August highlighted an AI-powered “Detective Border” system targeting Chinese-origin goods routed through third countries, while trade sources said CBP is also examining electricity and water consumption at overseas manufacturing facilities to compare reported production volumes and product values with facility capacity, potentially shifting enforcement from individual customs declarations toward broader supply-chain verification and making transshipment-based origin circumvention more difficult.
One market observer said any near-term bearish pressure on global prices should prove temporary, with the longer-term outlook for non-China polysilicon remaining positive as supply-chain diversification continues across the solar industry.
Meanwhile, the China Mono Premium, the OPIS assessment for mono-grade polysilicon used in n-type ingot production, was unchanged week on week at CNY 37.389 ($5.56)/kg, or CNY 0.079/W, but remains over 17% higher than in early August.
China’s polysilicon market continued to follow the pattern seen over the past two weeks. Manufacturers were still seeking to push prices higher, with some targeting above CNY 40/kg for new orders, but buyer acceptance continued to vary depending on existing inventories and downstream order conditions, according to trading sources.
One upstream source said the foundation for this round of price increases remains very weak, as some specialized wafer manufacturers had stocked up ahead of the latest price increase and therefore had contributed little to recent transactions. Meanwhile, buyers with long-term supply agreements settled at pre-increase prices for September delivery continued to transact at the original levels.
Another industry source said some buyers facing shortages and needing urgent deliveries, particularly those also requiring traceability documentation, had little choice but to accept around CNY 43/kg. However, overall volumes were limited, and the transactions were largely driven by a short-term spike in demand.
The futures market also pointed to limited confidence in the rally. One industry participant noted that September-delivery contracts on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange were trading at only CNY 37-38/kg, below the elevated spot offers, prompting some buyers to source September material through futures.
Market participants said production may be approaching a point where monthly output needs to be cut. According to the Silicon Branch of the China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association (CNMIA), China’s polysilicon output has risen for three consecutive months, from 92,900 metric tons (MT) in June to an expected level of more than 110,000 MT in August. Participants expect the growth to become increasingly difficult to sustain, with the price rally widely questioned.
One market participant said the onset of the dry season from October, which will reduce hydropower availability and raise production costs in some regions, could prompt manufacturers to lower operating rates. With buyers still unable to absorb large volumes above CNY 40/kg, manufacturers are unlikely to keep increasing production and inventories indiscriminately, the source added.
OPIS, a Dow Jones company, provides energy prices, news, data, and analysis on gasoline, diesel, jet fuel, LPG/NGL, coal, metals, and chemicals, as well as renewable fuels and environmental commodities. It acquired pricing data assets from Singapore Solar Exchange in 2022 and now publishes the
OPIS APAC Solar Weekly Report

title: 中国台湾拟于2028年重启马鞍山核电站
content:
中国台湾拟于2028年重启马鞍山核电站
中国台湾此前推进核能淘汰政策，但相关方向正在出现调整。台湾核安全委员会近日启动台湾电力公司提交的马鞍山核电站重启计划最终行政程序，该计划预计将进入正式审查阶段。按照目前进度，相关机组最早可能于2028年恢复运行。
马鞍山核电站又称台湾第三核能发电厂，位于屏东县恒春镇。该电站商业运行许可证已到期，此前停止商业运行。资料显示，马鞍山核电站过去约供应台湾5%的电力，是当地电力系统的重要电源之一。
台湾曾提出在2025年前停止核电运行，并以可再生能源等电源替代。近年，人工智能、半导体制造等产业用电需求持续增长，叠加电力供应稳定性和能源安全方面的压力，重启核电的讨论逐步升温。全球最大半导体代工企业台积电用电量约占台湾总用电量的9%，也使稳定供电议题受到更多关注。
去年8月，台湾曾就重启马鞍山核电站举行公投。投票结果显示，赞成票占比约74%，但因未达到法定门槛，公投案未获通过。尽管如此，支持重启核能的社会意见仍在扩大。
台湾核安全委员会相关负责人表示，后续将重点审查安全技术评估报告及配套文件，确认是否符合监管要求和核安全标准。清华大学核科学研究所所长叶宗光认为，相关机组有可能在2028年6月前重启，这显示台湾能源政策正从原先的核能淘汰路线转向更重视电力稳定供应。
台湾电力公司数据显示，天然气目前在台湾发电结构中占比最高，约为47.2%;煤电占比约31.1%;石油占比约1.4%。化石能源合计占比接近八成，可再生能源占比约11.9%。若马鞍山核电站恢复运行，预计将有助于减少部分燃煤发电需求，并对稳定电价形成支撑。

title: 海南儋州推进“核电入洋”“核汽入洋”支撑零碳园区建设
content:
海南儋州推进“核电入洋”“核汽入洋”支撑零碳园区建设
9月2日，开局起步十五五系列主题新闻发布会(市县层面第五场)——儋州市专场举行。儋州市有关负责人表示，“十五五”时期，儋州将围绕新型电力系统、新型能源体系和零碳园区低碳城市建设，推动清洁能源与临港产业深度耦合，全力争创国家新型电力系统示范地区。
根据发布内容，“十五五”期间，海南电网计划在儋州投资50亿元，打造“主—配—微”三级协同电网。到2030年，儋州将全面建成分层分区独立运行网架，推动“核电入洋”实现绿电就近消纳、全链条可溯源可核算，使全域电力碳排放因子降至0.05kgCO₂/kWh以下。
在核能综合利用方面，儋州将同步推进“核汽入洋”，依托昌江核电长距离供热，补齐零碳工业热源短板。相关安排将服务洋浦零碳园区培育和零碳城市建设，为重点用能企业节能降碳改造、存量产业低碳转型提供稳定能源支撑。
发布内容还提出，儋州将依托核电与风电、光伏等多能互补，构建零碳电力体系，并打通核能多元利用与绿氢转化链条，推动核电长距离供热与绿色甲醇、可持续航空燃料等项目落地。同时，当地将以“核电入洋”“核汽入洋”匹配高耗能产业低碳用能，建设双碳服务中心，提供碳足迹认证等全链条服务，推动石化新材料、装备制造与绿氢、绿电、核电协同发展。

title: 2026年第五次核电安全健康档案体系建设推进会召开
content:
2026-09-04 08:47 来源：国家核安全局
近日，核电安全健康档案体系建设工作组召开2026年第五次推进会及专题小组会议。工作组各成员单位及相关单位代表参加了会议。
会议就核电安全健康档案体系的信息化建设、算力配置、数据治理与共享、数智化应用研发等进展情况开展研讨，现场演示了监管侧及各集团健康档案信息系统功能实现情况，阶段性总结体系建设成效、梳理现存问题、部署近期工作任务。
会议指出，核电安全健康档案体系建设是推动核安全管理和监管机制转型的重要工作，当前数据治理初见成效，数据核查机制有效落地，应用场景开发工作持续推进，为后续体系持续完善创造了条件。会议要求，一要继续坚持目标导向、问题导向，聚焦体系基础功能，集中力量进一步针对性补齐短板，稳步推进体系建设;二要结合试点应用情况，及时开展复盘总结，全面梳理难点、堵点和薄弱环节，全流程改进体系运转效果;三要持续统筹推进数据对标入库、一线需求调研、场景开发落地等各项工作，全力保障核电安全健康档案体系高质量建成，助力我国核电厂运行安全和建造质量持续提升。

title: 英国劳斯莱斯SMR汽轮机关键部件将在纽卡斯尔生产
content:
英国劳斯莱斯SMR汽轮机关键部件将在纽卡斯尔生产
劳斯莱斯小型模块化反应堆公司 (Rolls-Royce SMR) 计划在英国北威尔士安格尔西岛格温内斯项目建设的首批三座小型模块化反应堆，其关键蒸汽轮机部件将在英国本土生产。西门子能源公司 (Siemens Energy) 位于纽卡斯尔的工厂将承担高压汽轮机和阀壳等部件制造任务。这也是欧洲首次为小型模块化反应堆在本土生产此类部件。
根据安排，西门子能源纽卡斯尔工厂还计划成为该公司服务劳斯莱斯SMR英国项目队列的关键部件服务中心。该工厂位于历史悠久的C.A.帕森斯工厂 (C.A. Parsons Works) 原址，其前身可追溯至查尔斯·帕森斯 (Charles Parsons) 爵士创办的涡轮机工厂。自1889年以来，该基地一直参与英国能源基础设施建设，其中包括为西坎布里亚郡卡尔德霍尔核电站 (Calder Hall Nuclear Power Station) 制造蒸汽轮机。卡尔德霍尔核电站于1956年开始发电，被视为世界首座商业核电站。
英国能源安全和净零排放大臣米娅塔·法恩布勒 (Miatta Fahnbulleh) 表示，在英国生产相关部件将有助于增强能源安全，降低英国对国际天然气市场波动的风险敞口，同时为本土工业创造新的出口机会。
英国商业、创新、科学与贸易大臣乔纳森·雷诺兹 (Jonathan Reynolds) 表示，这项安排预计将为纽卡斯尔创造和支持超过550个高质量就业岗位，并推动英国本土小型模块化反应堆供应链发展。
大英能源—核能公司 (Great British Energy – Nuclear) 首席执行官西蒙·罗迪 (Simon Roddy) 表示，关键部件将在纽卡斯尔制造，并用于北威尔士旗舰项目，显示英国不同地区均可参与小型模块化反应堆项目建设。他说，维持这类战略制造能力将有助于加强英国工业基础和国内供应链。
2025年2月，劳斯莱斯SMR选择西门子能源作为其全球汽轮机系统合作伙伴。按照双方合作安排，纽卡斯尔帕森斯原厂址将为英国格温内斯项目以及未来增长的小型模块化反应堆出口市场生产关键部件。
劳斯莱斯SMR首席执行官克里斯·乔勒顿 (Chris Cholerton) 表示，此次安排体现了公司推进本地化制造的承诺，并将部分原本可能在海外进行的工作转移至英国本土。西门子能源英国副总裁达伦·戴维森 (Darren Davidson) 表示，纽卡斯尔工厂将依托既有工程能力，为小型模块化反应堆生产新一代蒸汽轮机部件，并支持英国核能供应链建设。

title: 日本高滨核电站将运输1600桶低放射性废物
content:
日本高滨核电站将运输1600桶低放射性废物
关西电力公司 (Kansai Electric Power) 9月4日宣布，将把高滨核电站产生的低放射性废物运往青森县六所村的日本原燃公司 (Japan Nuclear Fuel Limited, JNFL) 低放射性废物埋设中心。
根据计划，低放射性废物专用运输船“青荣丸”号 (Seiei Maru) 将于9月5日靠泊高滨核电站，完成装载后于9月12日离港。若受气象等因素影响导致运输安排调整，关西电力公司将另行公布实际情况。
本次运输物为200个专用集装箱，内装1600只废物桶，均为充填固化体，不包括均质固化体。充填固化体是指核电站定期检查等作业过程中产生的金属、塑料、过滤器等固体低放射性废物，经分类后按需要进行切割、压缩或熔融处理，再装入废物桶，并使用水泥基充填材料固化形成的废物形态。
均质固化体则通常是将浓缩废液等低放射性废物与水泥、沥青等材料均匀混合后装桶固化。本次高滨核电站运输计划中未安排此类废物。

title: 土耳其阿库尤核电站启动WANO调试前同行评审
content:
土耳其阿库尤核电站启动WANO调试前同行评审
世界核电运营者协会莫斯科中心 (WANO-MC) 调试前同行评审的计划阶段，已在土耳其阿库尤核电站现场启动。该核电站由俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 承建，是土耳其首座在建核电站。
本次任务重点面向阿库尤核电站1号机组。评审结束后，世界核电运营者协会 (WANO) 将对该机组系统、设备及运行人员的运行准备状态开展独立评估，为机组后续安全运行提供参考。此次评审由WANO-MC机组人员绩效观察 (CPO) 和同行评审团队负责人王廷奎率队实施。
按照安排，专家组将采用CPO方法，对1号机组主控室操纵员的专业知识和操作技能进行评估。评审将在全范围模拟机 (FSS) 上开展，设置三类尽可能接近真实工况的受控场景，观察运行人员在机组管理、状态监测以及模拟设备故障处置中的表现。
评审人员还将结合场景演练结果，对运行流程、文件质量和应急程序进行分析，识别潜在改进领域。任务后期，CPO专家将与阿库尤核电站人员共同讨论相关评估报告。
阿库尤核电股份公司首席执行官谢尔盖·布茨基赫表示，WANO任务是电站调试前阶段的重要工作，不只是常规检查，也有助于提升运行团队能力、总结优势并明确改进方向。他说，与WANO合作使电站团队能够借鉴国际运行经验，学习并应用行业最佳实践。
WANO-MC专家组负责人表示，此次任务的主要目标，是评估运行人员在不同机组运行模式下的准备情况，包括运行扰动和设备故障条件下的处置能力。评估重点包括核安全原则执行情况、操纵员行动与协同、机组状态监测能力以及运行文件质量。根据现场观察，阿库尤核电站运行团队已对预设场景开展演练，能够识别偏差并采取相应措施，在切换备用控制系统时也能保持稳定操作。
阿库尤核电站规划建设4台机组，采用俄罗斯设计的第三代+ VVER反应堆，每台机组装机容量为1200兆瓦。该项目采用建设—拥有—运营 (BOO) 模式实施。世界核电运营者协会由全球核电站运营方组成，主要推动运行经验交流，促进核电站安全、可靠运行。

title: 印度私营核聚变托卡马克PRAGYA实现等离子体运行
content:
印度私营核聚变托卡马克PRAGYA实现等离子体运行
总部位于班加罗尔的深科技能源初创企业普拉诺斯聚变公司 (Pranos Fusion) 已在其实验装置 PRAGYA 中产生等离子体。该公司称，PRAGYA 是印度首个由私营企业开发的紧凑型托卡马克装置，这一进展标志着印度私营核聚变研发从设计制造阶段进入实验运行阶段。
PRAGYA 采用紧凑型、低纵横比托卡马克设计，主要用于产生、约束和控制等离子体。托卡马克通过强磁场将高温等离子体限制在环形真空室内，为未来实现轻原子核聚变创造条件。聚变反应的基本过程与太阳释放能量的机制相同，但工程实现仍面临等离子体约束、磁体、材料和控制系统等多重难题。
普拉诺斯聚变公司表示，PRAGYA 目前并非用于商业聚变发电，也不等同于实现净能量增益。该装置的定位是试验平台，用于验证更大型聚变装置所需的硬件、控制系统和运行经验。公司计划让 PRAGYA 运行近二十年，目标是每天开展 10 至 12 次实验性放电，年放电次数约 3000 次，从而积累等离子体行为、托卡马克设计和控制系统方面的数据。
PRAGYA 的建设周期约八个月。普拉诺斯聚变公司此前已开发用于托卡马克设计和控制的计算平台 JENGA，并推进聚变级高温超导磁体项目 MAGGA。按照该公司的技术路线，PRAGYA 将承担物理试验平台角色，用于测试等离子体控制技术、高温超导磁体、诊断设备及其他关键系统。公司目标是在 2027 年前推动高温超导磁体技术投入运行，并计划在 2030 年建设名为 PraniQ 的净增益聚变装置。
普拉诺斯聚变公司由绍里亚·考沙尔 (Shaurya Kaushal) 和罗山·乔治 (Roshan George) 于 2024 年创立，目前团队包括计算科学家、工程师和物理学家。该公司已在贾瓦哈拉尔·尼赫鲁高级科学研究中心 (JNCASR) 和等离子体研究所 (IPR) 联合孵化，借助相关科研基础设施和等离子体研究经验推进研发。
公司此前完成 680 万美元融资，本轮融资由 pi Ventures 和 Ankur Capital 共同领投，现有投资者 Industrial47 及天使投资人参与。普拉诺斯聚变公司曾表示，融资将用于加快其聚变技术栈研发，并推动 PRAGYA 等实验平台建设。
印度聚变研究长期主要依托政府科研机构及国际热核聚变实验堆 (ITER) 等国际合作项目。PRAGYA 的运行使印度聚变研发增加了私营部门参与的新路径。对普拉诺斯聚变公司而言，该装置不是终点，而是面向未来聚变反应堆的数据、工程和人才平台。

title: 美国完成HALEU TRISO燃料颗粒辐照后力学性能测量
content:
美国完成HALEU TRISO燃料颗粒辐照后力学性能测量
美国能源部橡树岭国家实验室 (Oak Ridge National Laboratory, ORNL) 研究人员已完成对辐照后高丰度低浓铀 (HALEU) TRISO燃料颗粒的力学性能测量，为下一代核燃料开发与鉴定提供了新的实验数据。
这是橡树岭国家实验室辐照燃料检验实验室中辐照后的AGR-2 TRISO燃料颗粒的光学横截面图像。图片来源：橡树岭国家实验室，美国能源部
TRISO燃料即三结构各向同性燃料，其颗粒外部包覆多层保护涂层，通常包括热解碳层和碳化硅层。这种结构使其具备较强的裂变产物滞留能力，被认为是先进反应堆，特别是高温气冷堆等堆型的重要燃料方案之一。了解这些涂层在辐照后的性能变化，是预测燃料在反应堆运行条件下表现的关键环节。
此次研究延续了ORNL今年早些时候对含HALEU的TRISO颗粒开展的中子散射测量工作。研究团队利用该实验室面向辐照材料和核燃料的专用压痕测试系统，对先进气冷反应堆燃料开发与鉴定计划 (AGRFP) 中TRISO颗粒的内外热解碳层及碳化硅层进行了力学性能测量。
在ORNL纳米力学实验室完成的测试显示，辐照后TRISO颗粒的硬度和刚度出现变化。其中，碳化硅层的模量和硬度有所降低，热解碳层也表现出相应变化。
ORNL颗粒燃料形态研究组研发助理研究员凯瑟琳·蒙托亚表示，这些测量结果有助于比较TRISO颗粒在原始制造状态下的性能，以及在不同温度和燃耗条件下经辐照后的性能。相关数据将用于改进核燃料性能模型，并为气冷堆技术的进一步应用提供支撑。

content:
俄罗斯国家原子能公司
VVER-1200

越南国会于2024年12月决定重启宁顺1号核电站项目。该项目曾于2016年暂停。根据越南总理今年3月访问俄罗斯期间签署的政府间协议，宁顺1号核电站将采用俄罗斯先进技术建设，并使用俄罗斯联邦提供的专项贷款。

title: 英美港口与航运机构研究核动力集装箱船跨大西洋部署
content:
英美港口与航运机构研究核动力集装箱船跨大西洋部署
英国船级社及专业咨询机构劳氏船级社 (Lloyd's Register)、丹麦航运企业马士基集团 (Maersk)、美国查尔斯顿港 (Port of Charleston) 和英国费利克斯托港 (Port of Felixstowe) 正在合作推进“粉红走廊”项目，研究核动力集装箱船在跨大西洋航线部署所涉及的安全与安保要求。
(图片来源：劳氏船级社)
该项目以一艘概念性核动力集装箱船为研究对象，重点分析其在南卡罗来纳州查尔斯顿港与英国萨福克郡费利克斯托港之间商业航线运行时，可能面临的港口准入条件和监管要求。研究内容包括船舶安全、安保措施、网络安全、应急响应、保险制度，以及海事监管与核能监管要求之间的衔接。
劳氏船级社表示，“粉红走廊”项目旨在为相关方提供一个结构化合作框架，帮助港口、航运企业和监管机构了解在设立核动力海上运输走廊之前，需要明确的实际要求、能力缺口和后续工作方向。项目第一阶段成果将为潜在第二阶段研究提供依据，后续可能进一步覆盖工程设计、监管安排、立法需求以及安全与安保框架等内容。
劳氏船级社全球集装箱船业务总监尼克·格罗斯 (Nick Gross) 表示，该联合开发项目是核技术进入商船运输领域的一项重要探索，将以务实合作方式研究核动力船舶安全运营所需的安保条件。他认为，航运企业、港口和船级社共同参与，反映出行业对核技术支持更可持续海事运营的关注正在上升。
费利克斯托港商务总监亚当·拉姆齐 (Adam Ramsey) 表示，费利克斯托港作为英国规模最大、最繁忙的集装箱港口，将为该项目提供运营层面的实践经验，并支持行业探索更具长期可持续性的全球贸易方案。南卡罗来纳州港务局 (South Carolina Ports) 船舶运营和承运商销售总监汤姆·博伊尔 (Tom Boyle) 表示，查尔斯顿港希望研究更具创新性、经济性和可持续性的货运方式，“粉红走廊”概念项目正是围绕核动力海上走廊的可行性展开。
此次合作延续了科尔电力公司 (Core Power)、马士基集团、劳氏船级社和荷兰鹿特丹港 (Port of Rotterdam) 此前开展的一项研究。该研究聚焦核动力集装箱船停靠欧盟港口时的安全、运营和监管问题，并指出，核动力船舶进港面临的主要障碍并非技术本身，而在于地方与国际监管协调、治理安排、风险管理整合以及公众接受度。
航运业每年消耗约3.5亿吨化石燃料，碳排放量约占全球总量的3%。国际海事组织 (IMO) 已批准新的温室气体减排目标，力争在2050年前后实现净零排放。劳氏船级社此前发布报告称，核能有望通过零排放推进方式改变海运业，同时延长船舶使用寿命，并减少燃料供应和加注基础设施建设的不确定性，但商业化应用仍需解决监管与安全问题。
目前，民用船舶核能应用已成为多个国际机构和企业研究的方向。国际海事组织正在修订《核动力船舶安全规则》，国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 近期启动“海上应用”计划，旨在支持海事行业探索小型模块化反应堆在民用船舶动力和海上能源供应中的应用。

title: 瑞典首座新建核反应堆或于2030年代中期投运
content:
瑞典首座新建核反应堆或于2030年代中期投运
瑞典能源和工业部长、基督教民主党 (KD) 领导人埃巴·布施 (Ebba Busch) 9月3日在一场公开听证中表示，瑞典首座新建核反应堆可能在2030年代中期投入使用。
在被问及新核电机组何时能够投运时，布施给出的时间是“2030年代中期”。她同时表示，新建核电项目不会依靠国家直接出资建设。
不过，瑞典政府此前已为新核电建设准备了支持框架。相关安排可能涉及数千亿瑞典克朗规模的资金支持，其中包括贷款以及总额约4000亿瑞典克朗的电价担保。布施称，这确实是一笔巨大资金，但其性质是贷款和价格对冲安排，针对的是重要的基础设施。
围绕瑞典大瀑布电力公司 (Vattenfall) 在林哈尔斯核电站区域推进的新核电项目，瑞典国家层面还将成为维德贝里电力公司 (Videberg Kraft) 的重要所有方。该公司负责推进Vattenfall在林哈尔斯相关项目的开发。
当被问及瑞典政府是否会在瓦罗半岛建设新的核电站时，布施作出肯定回应。她表示，新核电项目对瑞典而言是一项有利投资，有助于增强国家在不稳定时期的能源保障能力。

title: 俄罗斯滨海边疆区核电站计划2031年前并网
content:
俄罗斯滨海边疆区核电站计划2031年前并网
俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 计划在2031年前将滨海边疆区核电站接入电网。该公司首席执行官阿列克谢·利哈乔夫 (Alexey Likhachev) 9月3日在东方经济论坛 (Eastern Economic Forum) 期间表示，项目正在按既定目标推进。
利哈乔夫说，Rosatom正努力确保该核电站首台机组在2027年底前实现“第一罐混凝土”浇筑。按照当前设想，项目目标是在2031年实现并网发电，并在2032年全面投入运行。
他同时表示，远东地区特别是滨海边疆区在核能利用方面尚缺乏足够经验，仍需逐步建立相关专业能力和工程支撑体系。Rosatom将继续推进项目建设，以服务当地电力系统需求。

title: 俄罗斯拟在摩尔曼斯克附近建设浮动核电站生产设施
content:
俄罗斯拟在摩尔曼斯克附近建设浮动核电站生产设施
俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 正考虑在摩尔曼斯克附近建设自有生产设施，用于完成浮动核电站建造。该公司认为，随着相关订单增加，现有合作伙伴的产能可能难以满足后续需求。
波罗的海造船厂 (Baltic Shipyard) 是俄罗斯国家原子能公司的重要合作方之一。“罗蒙诺索夫院士”号浮动核电站以及4艘22220型“北极”级核动力破冰船均由该船厂建造。目前，双方仍保持密切合作，波罗的海造船厂相当一部分订单与俄罗斯国家原子能公司的项目有关。
俄罗斯国家原子能公司首席执行官阿列克谢·利哈乔夫表示，公司正在评估建设自有生产设施的方案，项目投资预计将达到数百亿卢布。他说，22220型核动力破冰船批量建造是公司的重要任务之一，原因是市场对破冰船的需求持续增长。与此同时，公司也在分析浮动核电站项目的建设前景，目前相关计划涉及数十座浮动核电站。
利哈乔夫表示，在与合作伙伴合作效率更高的领域，公司将继续采用合作模式;在确有必要建立自有生产能力的领域，公司也会推进相应布局。
他介绍，摩尔曼斯克附近是一个经过审慎考虑的选址方向。该地区靠近俄罗斯核动力破冰船船队及港口基础设施，同时临近大型城市，并具备通向海洋的条件。
此前，俄罗斯国家原子能公司曾讨论将波罗的海造船厂并入公司的可能性。不过，该造船厂管理层决定继续留在联合造船集团 (USC) 体系内，俄罗斯国家原子能公司接受了这一决定。此后，该公司的相关订单数量继续增加。

title: 韩国首尔科技大学与斗山能源深化核设计合作
content:
韩国首尔科技大学与斗山能源深化核设计合作
首尔科技大学 (SeoulTech) 与斗山能源公司 (Doosan Enerbility) 近日签署合作备忘录，双方将围绕下一代核电站、小型模块化反应堆 (SMR) 以及核心核设备技术等领域开展产学研合作，提升核设计技术竞争力，并共同培养专业科研人才。
签约仪式于9月2日在首尔科技大学举行。斗山能源公司核设计高级副总裁徐永彬 (Seo Young-bin)、部门主管金钟仁 (Kim Jong-in) 以及校方相关负责人出席仪式。
根据合作备忘录，双方将整合高校科研能力与企业在核电站设计方面的工程经验，建立面向长期合作的基础框架。该协议并非确定具体科研项目，而是为后续识别、论证和推进联合研究、技术开发及人才培养项目提供机制支撑。
双方计划重点评估在核心核设备技术、创新设计和可靠性评估等方向开展研究合作与委托服务的可行性;推动技术和人员交流，共同利用研究设施;合作建设研究基础设施和研究中心;围绕相关项目培养专业人才;并通过研讨会、专题讨论会等形式开展学术与技术交流。
首尔科技大学表示，将依托自身工程研究基础，结合斗山能源在大型核电站设计领域积累的产业经验，搭建支持大型核电站、下一代核电站和小型模块化反应堆设计与评估技术发展的产学研合作平台。双方希望通过联合研究和人员交流，将产业技术需求与科研教育体系相衔接，培养具备核设计和可靠性评估实践能力的研究人员。
首尔科技大学校长金东焕表示，此次合作为大学研究能力与产业界专业经验结合提供了基础，有助于提升下一代核电站和小型模块化反应堆领域的技术竞争力，并培养面向未来核工业的人才。校方将继续扩大与产业界的务实合作，服务韩国核工业竞争力提升。

title: 亚美尼亚将与俄罗斯原子能公司讨论新建核电站方案
content:
亚美尼亚将与俄罗斯原子能公司讨论新建核电站方案
亚美尼亚总理尼科尔·帕希尼扬 (Nikol Pashinyan) 9月3日在新闻发布会上表示，俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 总裁阿列克谢·利哈乔夫 (Alexey Likhachev) 将于9月访问亚美尼亚，双方将在亚美尼亚境内讨论新建核电站的可能方案。
帕希尼扬称，亚方预计利哈乔夫此访将提出俄罗斯方面关于在亚美尼亚新建核电站的具体设想。他表示，亚美尼亚在选择核电项目时将重点考虑经济性和方案报价，目标是获得“性价比最高”的建设方案。
今年5月，俄罗斯方面曾表示，已向亚美尼亚提交一份核电站设计方案，可满足该国长期能源需求。随后，帕希尼扬确认，亚美尼亚已收到Rosatom提供的大型核电站设计方案，该方案旨在保障亚美尼亚未来多年的能源供应。
帕希尼扬同时指出，亚美尼亚政府更倾向于建设一座模块化核电站。现阶段，亚方仍在对不同技术路线和建设方案进行比较。

title: 俄罗斯拟在雅库特建设浮动小型核电站
content:
俄罗斯拟在雅库特建设浮动小型核电站
俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 核能第一副总经理、原子能建设出口股份公司 (JSC Atomstroyexport) 总裁安德烈·彼得罗夫 (Andrey Petrov) 表示，俄罗斯能源部已支持在萨哈共和国(雅库特)推进浮动式小型核电站方案。
彼得罗夫在东方经济论坛期间表示，按照相关总体规划，雅库特小型核电站需在2031年前建成。目前正在研究的新方案，是将原先的陆上核电站调整为浮动式核电站。他说，浮动式方案造价更低、建设周期更短，可满足雅库特当前约106兆瓦的电力需求。
此前，萨哈共和国(雅库特)行政长官艾森·尼古拉耶夫 (Aysen Nikolayev) 曾谈及远东地区特别是雅库特的能源供应问题。彼得罗夫称，浮动式小型核电站正是针对当地能源保障需求提出的解决路径之一。
雅库特小型核电站项目原计划采用最新的RITM-200N反应堆装置。Rosatom与萨哈共和国(雅库特)政府于2019年签署相关协议。按照原方案，该项目拟建设在亚纳河沿岸的乌斯季扬斯基区，靠近乌斯季库伊加镇，建成后有望成为俄罗斯首座采用新型设计的陆上小型核电站。此次方案调整意味着该项目后续建设形式可能发生变化。

title: 韩国韩光核电站两台机组焊接规程不合规
content:
韩国韩光核电站两台机组焊接规程不合规
韩国水力原子能公司 (KHNP) 韩光核电站总部近日确认，韩光核电站1号和2号机组在设备冷却水换热器维护中，曾使用未进行冲击试验的焊接工艺规程 (WPS)。经追溯检查，自2007年更换相关换热器以来的14项维修作业中，有6项存在同类不合规情况。
此次问题是在韩光1号机组第28次计划性预防性维护期间发现的。检查显示，用于设备冷却水换热器水室维修的部分焊接工艺规程不符合要求，涉及1号和2号机组冷却系统中换热器水室内部磨损区域的维修作业。
韩光核电站总部表示，焊接作业本应按照美国机械工程师协会 (ASME) 规范执行。此次误用的原因，是相关人员在解读ASME规范时，误判该焊接工艺规程可以免除冲击试验。该总部同时称，对既往作业的审查显示，经过冲击试验的焊接工艺规程与未经过冲击试验的焊接工艺规程，在实际维护涉及的各项变量上并无差异。
韩光核电站总部计划对能够确认具体位置的既往维修区域实施返工;对于难以确定问题位置的区域，将通过更换部件处理。相关措施计划于明年4月前完成。该总部还表示，已改进相关程序，将维护和更换活动检查清单、部件检查清单纳入计划阶段管理，并要求在不适用技术标准的情况下明确记录依据。
韩光核电站方面解释，涉事换热器的功能是降低输送至主要设备的冷却水温度，与反应堆安全或放射性物质泄漏没有直接关联。不过，由于核电站维护作业规程执行不当已被确认，相关返工或部件更换仍需推进。
按原计划，韩光1号和2号机组将于明年上半年接受继续运行审查。其中，1号机组计划自2025年12月起停止发电并开展设备改进工作;2号机组原计划于本月11日停止运行，实施类似设备维护。此前，韩国核安全监管部门曾提出，将通过简化监管审议程序，缩短接近设计寿期末期核电机组继续运行的审议周期。

title: 俄罗斯称正推进小型核电站建设
content:
俄罗斯称正推进小型核电站建设

title: 匈牙利保克什二期核电项目或需重大调整
content:
俄罗斯国家原子能公司
VVER-1200
据熟悉匈牙利核工业及保克什二期核电项目讨论情况的人士透露，由彼得·马扎尔 (Peter Magyar) 领导的匈牙利新政府认为，基于俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 设计的保克什二期核电项目，只有在进行重大调整后才有可能继续推进。
知情人士称，受伦理、技术、制裁限制、许可程序以及现有合同条款等因素影响，保克什二期项目难以按原有安排继续实施。不过，业内人士也认为，因短期情绪或阶段性挫折而直接放弃该项目并不合适。如果能够引入更多参与方，尤其是西方企业，共同解决替代零部件供应、欧盟层面沟通协调以及许可程序推进等问题，项目仍存在继续实施的空间。
目前，匈牙利经济能源部和保克什二期项目新管理层正对项目进行审查，范围包括相关协议和合同。匈牙利政府正在研究在西方企业更多参与的情况下继续推进项目的可能性，同时并未完全排除放弃建设俄罗斯制造的VVER-1200型反应堆、转向小型模块化反应堆 (SMR) 的选项。
据悉，匈牙利总理尚未收到经济能源部提交的最终方案，并要求对项目现状进行全面评估。匈牙利政府也认识到，如果终止与Rosatom的协议，可能面临数十亿欧元赔偿风险，而俄方在合同法律层面具有较强地位。因此，布达佩斯方面在作出最终决定前仍需审慎权衡。
Rosatom此前表示，保克什二期核电项目施工正按照计划和匈牙利承包商批准的进度推进。今年2月5日，5号机组浇筑首罐混凝土。按照国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 标准，该项目由此正式进入“在建核电站”阶段，标志着工程从前期准备转入主体建设。
保克什二期核电站建设依据俄匈两国2014年签署的政府间协议，以及建设两台VVER-1200型反应堆机组的三份基础合同推进。该项目预计投资125亿欧元，原计划约80%资金来自俄罗斯贷款，两台新机组计划于21世纪30年代上半叶投入运行。
保克什核电站位于布达佩斯以南约100公里的多瑙河畔，现有4台VVER-440型反应堆，于20世纪80年代在苏联援助下建成投运。目前，该电站承担匈牙利约45%的发电量和36%的电力消费。保克什二期建成后，保克什核电站总装机容量预计将由目前约2000兆瓦增至4400兆瓦。

title: 韩国韩蔚核电站6号机组开展辐射应急演练
content:
韩国韩蔚核电站6号机组开展辐射应急演练
韩国水力原子能公司 (KHNP) 韩蔚核电站近日对6号机组开展全面辐射灾害预防演练，检验辐射紧急情况下的应急响应体系和现场处置能力。
据韩蔚核电站方面介绍，演练于9月3日举行，按照韩国核安全研究院 (KINS) 制定的评估指南，并依据《国家辐射应急预案》组织实施。此次演练方案未提前公开，评估方式也作出调整，重点核查机组在实际应急场景下的响应能力。
演练中，韩蔚核电站6号机组全体应急人员参与处置。现场模拟控制区内发生人员伤亡事故，组织开展医疗救援，并使用一台3.2兆瓦移动发电机，对应急设施运行能力进行检查。
韩蔚核电站表示，此次演练对人员应急技能、跨部门协同响应机制以及应急设施运行状态进行了综合检验。韩蔚核电站厂长李勇熙称，电站将根据演练中发现的问题进行整改，并通过持续培训提升应急响应能力。

title: 美国纳米核能KRONOS MMR主氦气循环器进入详细设计阶段
content:
美国纳米核能KRONOS MMR主氦气循环器进入详细设计阶段
美国纳米核能公司 (NANO Nuclear Energy Inc.) 9月3日宣布，其KRONOS MMR能源系统主氦气循环器开发取得新进展。该公司与贝克休斯公司 (Baker Hughes) 旗下豪顿公司 (Howden) 的工程合作已从初步工程设计推进至详细设计阶段。
主氦气循环器是KRONOS MMR能源系统的关键机械子系统，主要用于驱动氦冷却剂在反应堆内循环，将堆芯产生的热量高效传递至后续系统。该设备的性能直接关系到反应堆热工表现、整体效率以及长期运行可靠性。
根据纳米核能公司披露的信息，豪顿公司负责主氦气循环器的工程设计，并结合其在氦气涡轮机械和高温气冷反应堆技术方面的经验，为KRONOS MMR能源系统开发定制化方案。目前，豪顿公司已完成关键工程评估、详细三维设计模型、相关工程分析，并与纳米核能公司的工程团队进行了正式设计评审。
纳米核能公司表示，双方下一阶段工作将包括部件鉴定、材料与性能测试、持续设计优化以及制造计划制定。这些工作将为主氦气循环器子系统的性能验证、可制造性评估以及与KRONOS MMR能源系统的集成奠定基础。
此次进展发布前，纳米核能公司还曾宣布与富迪公司 (Fortil) 推进KRONOS MMR能源系统燃料处理与存储系统设计合作。该系统用于在反应堆运行过程中处理、存储和管理核燃料，是KRONOS MMR能源系统中的另一项关键子系统。
纳米核能公司首席执行官詹姆斯·沃克 (James Walker) 表示，主氦气循环器进入详细设计阶段，是KRONOS MMR能源系统开发过程中的一项工程节点，将支持该项目继续推进原型建造、监管许可和未来部署相关工作。
KRONOS MMR能源系统是一种固定式高温气冷微型模块化反应堆。纳米核能公司称，该项目目前正就施工许可预申请事项与美国核管理委员会 (NRC) 沟通，并与伊利诺伊大学厄巴纳—香槟分校开展合作。

title: KN能源公司加入波罗的海能源倡议
content:
波罗的海能源倡议
小型模块化反应堆
国际能源码头运营商立陶宛KN能源公司 (KN Energies) 9月3日宣布，已加入由波兰奥伦集团 (ORLEN) 发起的波罗的海能源倡议。该倡议目前汇集了北欧和中欧9个国家的14家能源企业和机构，计划通过区域合作提升波罗的海地区能源安全、基础设施韧性和产业竞争力。
根据相关安排，波罗的海能源倡议将作为跨国合作平台，推动成员共享专业经验，并联合开发具有区域影响力的能源项目。合作重点包括海上风电、液化天然气和生物液化天然气市场融合、区域氢能市场建设、碳运输与封存，以及小型模块化反应堆开发。参与方还将共同争取欧盟项目资金及其他国际融资支持。
签署该协议的机构来自波兰、芬兰、瑞典、丹麦、德国、立陶宛、拉脱维亚、爱沙尼亚和挪威。除KN能源公司和奥伦集团外，参与方还包括爱沙尼亚能源公司 (Eesti Energia)、埃内菲特公司 (Enefit)、富腾公司 (Fortum)、挪威船级社能源系统 (DNV Energy Systems)、托普索公司 (Topsoe)、西门子能源 (Siemens Energy)、阿德文公司 (Adven)、斯特迪能源公司 (Steady Energy)、P2X解决方案公司 (P2X Solutions)、拉脱维亚电力公司 (Latvenergo)、芬兰天然气管网公司 (Gasgrid Finland) 和维斯塔斯公司 (Vestas)。
该倡议还将推动成员在监管事务、投资安排和战略项目支持机制等方面形成共同意见，以便在与欧洲相关机构沟通时更集中地表达区域能源行业需求。成员认为，统一协调有助于释放波罗的海地区在清洁能源、低碳燃料和新型核能技术方面的开发潜力。
能源基础设施保护也是合作内容之一。参与方将围绕关键基础设施保护、网络安全、应急准备以及应对物理和复合型威胁等领域交流经验，并共同评估可提升能源系统韧性的项目及潜在融资渠道。

title: 日本泊核电站3号机组重启审查仍需补充消防安全文件
content:
日本泊核电站3号机组重启审查仍需补充消防安全文件
9月3日，日本泊核电站3号机组重启计划召开审查会议。日本原子能规制委员会 (NRA) 指出，北海道电力公司 (Hokkaido Electric Power) 就消防安全措施提交的说明仍存在需要进一步确认的问题，要求其补充更详细的评估材料。
泊核电站3号机组重启所需的设备设计和施工计划自去年以来一直处于审查阶段。当前审查重点之一，是在厂内发生火灾的情况下，相关作业人员是否具备充分、可行的疏散措施。
在当天会议上，北海道电力公司代表说明了修订后的消防安全措施。该公司称，已对照《消防法》相关标准，确认火灾发生时拟使用的灭火剂以及人员疏散方法具备安全性。
对此，原子能规制委员会认为，仅说明“已经确认”并不足以支撑审查结论，要求北海道电力公司提交更细化的文件，说明具体评估方法、审查过程及其适当性。委员会表示，相关内容仍有必要进行追加审查。
北海道电力公司此前曾提出，泊核电站3号机组将“最快于明年”恢复运行，并计划在本月向原子能规制委员会提交通过审查所需的最终修订文件。按目前情况看，相关文件提交时间可能推迟，后续追加审查将对机组重启进度产生多大影响，仍有待观察。
