title: ‘Unfair Trade’: Automakers Push Congress To Ban Chinese Cars In The U.S.
content:
‘Unfair Trade’: Automakers Push Congress To Ban Chinese Cars In The U.S.
A major auto industry lobby group wants Congress to put an end to Chinese imports before they even start.
- Car makers in the U.S. want Congress to ban Chinese cars before the end of the year.
- There’s not a single Chinese-branded car for sale in the U.S, but a major lobby group wants that to become permanent law.
- The Alliance for Automotive Innovation sent a letter to Congress, saying that Chinese automakers are dumping subsidized vehicles around the world.
Chinese-branded cars are gaining steam across the world, except for the United States, where there’s not a single Chinese car for sale. And now, a major lobby group wants legislators to keep China’s connected cars out of the U.S. for good, as soon as possible.
The Alliance for Automotive Innovation, which represents dozens of carmakers with a U.S. presence, including General Motors, Ford, Honda, BMW, Toyota, and Volvo, sent a letter to Congress, urging lawmakers to permanently ban Chinese cars from reaching the country before the year ends.
BYD, China's biggest carmaker, has seen increased success in Europe with its growing portfolio of EVs and PHEVs.
“Right now, Chinese automakers are dumping subsidized vehicles with connected software and hardware around the world,” said John Bozzella, the group’s CEO and the person who signed the letter. “China is capturing market share in Europe, Australia, Southeast Asia, Mexico, and South America with vehicles capable of collecting, processing, and transmitting sensitive vehicle and consumer data to the Chinese Communist Party.”
To be clear, Chinese-made vehicles already face a couple of roadblocks, preventing them from hitting American roads. A 100% import tariff hikes prices even before they hit U.S. shores, and existing Commerce Department rules restrict Chinese software and hardware in connected vehicles–the same rules that stopped Polestar from doing business stateside.
So, why the urgency now? Bozzella said that passing legislation barring Chinese vehicles from the U.S. market “will send a clear and bipartisan message that China’s strategy to dominate global automotive manufacturing will be met with a national security response from the American government.”
Among the worries backing up the initiative is the fact that Chinese-made cars could send sensitive information back to Beijing. However, the fact that China has subsidized its auto industry for years is also at play. The move allowed local companies to offer cars that are significantly cheaper than the competition, which has helped big names get an edge in the global market.
All this being said, it has been well documented that Chinese cars–mostly EVs–are better than their Western competitors, which doesn’t bode well for the American auto industry. Just like Japanese brands became household names in the 1970s thanks to their better build quality and lower fuel consumption, the same could happen today with China’s offerings. But not if they’re locked out through legislation.

title: This 7-Seat EV Went 582 Miles On A Charge. But There’s A Catch
content:
A production-spec Skoda Peaq traveled 582 miles on one charge, driving on secondary roads and hypermiling to achieve it.
Photo by:
7:00am ET
The seven-seat Škoda Peaq traveled 582 miles, beating its WLTP range by 45%.
Secondary roads, dry weather, and careful hypermiling made the record possible.
The Peaq averaged 9.2 kWh/100 km.
We all know by this point that official range ratings are more like suggestions than hard-and-fast guarantees. However, beating a car's WLTP range by almost half is still remarkable, and that’s what a production-spec
Škoda Peaq
90 did on a carefully calculated hypermiling run.
Two of the manufacturer's employees drove the SUV for 582 miles (936 km) without recharging, which is 179 miles (289 km)—or 45%—more than its WLTP range of 402 miles (647 km). This was achieved in a standard vehicle with a 91-kilowatt-hour battery pack and a usable capacity of 86 kWh, with no modifications.
Skoda did it by using AI to plot a route from Mladá Boleslav, where the car was built, into the Netherlands that completely avoided high-speed highway driving. It chose secondary roads with light traffic, and drivers maintained as constant a speed as traffic allowed, doing their best to avoid hard acceleration, heavy braking, and complete stops.
Škoda notes that dry weather also helped, acknowledging that wet roads would have made the result impossible. It didn’t disclose the car’s average speed. It did, however, reveal that the Peaq averaged 9.2 kWh/100 km, or about 6.8 miles/kWh.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The journey began at noon on Tuesday and ended on Wednesday afternoon, with multiple driver changes and an overnight rest. Completing the trip quickly wasn’t a priority. The original destination was Amsterdam, around 530 miles (850 km) from the starting point.
However, after reaching the Netherlands with more charge remaining than expected, the crew decided to extend the journey by another 28 miles (50 km) and ended up in the seaside resort of Zandvoort. For the last few miles of the journey, the car showed no remaining range and 0% state of charge, but it was driven until it wouldn’t move anymore.
Gallery: Skoda Peaq 90 Efficiency Run
BMW previously attempted
something similar
iX3 50 xDrive
. Its engineers covered 1,007.7 km, or 626 miles, from
Debrecen, Hungary
, to Munich, arriving with 2% charge remaining. BMW says its team also mostly used country roads, kept the climate control, seat heating, and infotainment off, and stopped overnight.
It also sounds like the range test General Motors did last year, when its engineers
drove a Chevrolet Silverado EV

title: BYD’s Electric Kei Car Was Driven In Japan. It Fits Right In
content:
This early English-language of BYD's kei EV reveals a roomy, comfy and thoughtfully engineered EV that feels right at home in Japan
Photo by:
Everything Electric APAC
6:59am ET
An early drive finds the $13,000 BYD Racco roomy, comfortable and remarkably well suited to Japanese roads.
It’s the first ground-up, mainstream kei passenger car developed by an overseas automaker.
It matches the Nissan Sakura’s power, but with less torque, yet offers up to 199 miles of range, versus the Nissan’s 112 miles.
Chinese automakers typically enter foreign markets trying to overwhelm rivals with their cars’ power, tech, and range. But BYD couldn’t use that playbook with
the Racco
because Japan’s kei-car rules tightly restrict dimensions and power output, forcing BYD to try to win through packaging, practicality, and attention to local tastes.
One of the first English-language drives of the Racco suggests BYD may have just pulled it off.
Everything Electric APAC
presenter Elliot Richards went to Himeji, Japan, where BYD lent him a Racco for the day.
This wasn’t a conventional press launch, and Elliot says he paid for the trip himself, so the fact that he calls the Racco an “absolute banger” holds more weight than if it had been the result of a fully paid (and often highly curated) official media drive.
What seemed to impress him most was how thoroughly BYD embraced the kei-car brief. The Racco’s tall, boxy body and power-sliding rear doors make it exceptionally easy to enter, while its high seating position gives great all-around visibility. Despite its tiny footprint, the host found the rear legroom better than in many much larger SUVs and described the back seats as “supremely comfortable.”
The Racco has a highly modular interior with seats that can also be folded, reclined, or flipped forward to accommodate unusually tall cargo. With them folded, the Racco becomes a tiny electric van with a long, nearly flat floor and a useful, square cargo area.
As with any kei car, the cabin is pretty basic, but Elliot says it is one of BYD’s best interiors precisely because the company resisted the urge to fill it with gimmicks. Front seat comfort is rated excellent, and the vehicle is easy to operate thanks to physical climate controls and a small touchscreen with Apple CarPlay.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
On the road, it feels remarkably similar to its main rival,
the Nissan Sakura
. The steering is reasonably direct but slightly soft, while the brakes were sharper than Elliot says he would have liked. Acceleration is merely adequate, but with low urban speed limits and narrow streets, he concluded that it has all the performance it needs.
BYD’s effort with the Racco compares well with the Sakura, Japan’s best-selling EV for four consecutive years through 2025. Both have exactly the same footprint and power output dictated by kei car regulations. However, the Racco stands 5.7 inches (145 mm) taller than the Nissan.
More BYD Stories
The Sakura features a 20-kilowatt-hour battery with 112 miles (180 km) of WLTC range. The Racco offers either a 22.4-kWh pack with 130 miles (210 km) of range, or a much larger 35.8-kWh battery capable of 199 miles (320 km). The Nissan counters with 144 lb-ft (195 Nm) of torque, compared with the BYD’s 118 lb-ft (160 Nm), which should make it feel noticeably nippier to drive.
The Racco starts at around $13,000 before Japan’s almost $1,000 clean car incentive has been factored in, although the Sakura can become slightly cheaper after Japan’s more generous subsidy for domestic models is applied.

title: Watch Tesla’s Cybercab Carry Passengers Through Austin. It’s Almost Boring
content:
Tesla's self-driving taxi completed an uneventful trip in Austin with no steering wheel, pedals, or apparent human intervention.
Photo by:
Sawyer Merritt/YouTube
6:08am ET
Tesla’s steering-wheel-free Cybercab is now carrying passengers on public roads in Austin.
A 14-minute video shows a smooth, quiet ride and just one stumble from the car's AI voice assistant.
The trip is encouraging, but one geofenced Austin ride proves little about tougher cities or conditions.
After years of promises, prototypes and demonstrations in controlled environments, Tesla’s purpose-built Cybercab has finally started transporting passengers on public roads. An early video from inside suggests that the most radical Tesla yet, which has no physical controls, can deliver a remarkably ordinary-looking ride.
Longtime Tesla-focused content creator
Sawyer Merritt
uploaded a 14-minute video of himself and his wife riding
in a Cybercab
as it drives them through Austin. It looks like it’s a pretty simple process. Once both passengers are inside, the butterfly doors close automatically and you tap on “Start Ride” on the central screen.
The Cybercab then pulled away smoothly and began making its way to the destination. The drive itself was almost eerily uneventful. The Cybercab negotiated the filmed portion of the route without hesitation, sudden braking, or abrupt maneuvers. Its suspension also seemed to absorb a speed bump smoothly, and Merritt praised its ride quality.
He describes the ride as quiet, soft, and “perfectly boring,” which is exactly what you want from a driverless taxi.
Most of the video focuses on the in-cabin experience. The two-seat bench slides forward and back as a whole, the backrests can be reclined, and there is a lot more legroom than the Cybercab’s compact exterior might suggest. Riders control the climate, seats, doors, and entertainment through the huge central screen, which measures around 21 inches.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
The only stumble of the entire ride came from Grok, which mistook a request to adjust the cabin temperature for a destination change.
Merritt goes on to say the Cybercab drives better than a human and that it’s already so good it doesn’t need further development. However, he is a known enthusiastic Tesla supporter, so this should be treated strictly as one fan's opinion, and one Cybercab ride is nowhere near enough to make such an assessment, no matter how good it was.
The Cybercab still needs to prove itself in inclement weather, avoiding roadworks, aggressive driving around it, or just the genuine unpredictability of traffic. Successfully navigating a limited, geofenced section of Austin does not prove it can handle New York City’s denser traffic, heavier pedestrian activity, and constant road obstructions.
More On This
The start of passenger rides in the Cybercab is still a significant milestone for Tesla and the entire driverless ride-hailing scene. The
first production Cybercab
rolled off the line in February. By June, Tesla was
testing a steering-wheel-free version
on Austin roads, albeit with a safety monitor in the passenger seat. Just before this week’s launch, it
registered 45 Cybercabs
in Texas.
Merritt’s footage still shows something pretty important: the Cybercab is no longer just a concept or prototype. Actual passengers are now sitting inside while it drives itself and, on this occasion, nothing particularly exciting happened, which is encouraging.

title: Tesla's New EV Doesn't Have Brake Lines Or Brake Fluid. Here’s How It Stops
content:
The Tesla Cybercab Has No Brake Lines Or Brake Fluid. Here’s How It Stops
The two-seater doesn’t have a steering wheel or pedals. As a result, controlling the brakes and steering needed a rethink.
- Tesla has unveiled the production version of the Cybercab two-door EV.
- The car doesn’t have a steering wheel or pedals, but it also lacks a traditional braking system.
- There is no brake fluid, and there are no brake lines going to the wheels.
The Tesla Cybercab is officially here, with the first production models scheduled to hit Austin streets later today, as part of the company’s growing Robotaxi fleet. The smallest passenger EV in Tesla’s portfolio was officially launched last night during a private, closed-door event where several interesting tidbits of information were made available for the first time.
We already knew that the Cybercab doesn’t have a steering wheel or pedals, despite the potential regulatory roadblocks associated with this design decision. However, what we didn’t know was that the two-seater EV also doesn’t have a traditional braking system.
According to multiple reports from people who attended last night’s event, the Tesla Cybercab doesn’t use brake fluid and doesn’t have brake lines or a central master cylinder. Instead, each caliper has an individual electronically controlled actuator that applies braking force to the rotor.
This type of braking system is called dry brake-by-wire, and the Cybercab is one of the first production cars in the world fitted with it–China’s Chery Exceed EX7 debuted with a similar system in April. Other vehicles have brake-by-wire systems, too, but they’re typically a dual-layer setup with an electronic brake controller backed by a hydraulic master cylinder that interprets electronic signals.
Because the Cybercab doesn’t have a steering wheel, the steering system is also electronic, without a steering column. The steer-by-wire box is located at the rear of the front-mounted electric motor.
According to Tesla CEO Elon Musk, having electric brakes avoids the complexity of a hydraulic system because there’s no need to route plumbing all around the vehicle. That said, cables still need to be routed to the calipers, but the approach might shave some pennies off the final build because it eliminates several individual components, including the brake fluid reservoir, brake lines, and hydraulic brake master cylinder.
The braking system’s supplier hasn’t been disclosed, but there are just a handful of companies that currently offer electronic braking systems, including Brembo, ZF, and Bosch. Besides lowering manufacturing costs, going for a fluid-less braking system allows the car’s brain to apply different forces to each wheel when braking, whereas a traditional hydraulic system will send the same pressure to each caliper.
Coincidence or not, Brembo has used several Tesla vehicles to showcase its Sensify electronic braking system in the past, but there’s no confirmation that the Italian manufacturer is behind the Cybercab's braking system.

title: Tesla’s Cybercab Is Finally Giving Paid Robotaxi Rides. Here’s What It Can And Can’t Do
content:
Tesla’s Cybercab Is Finally Giving Paid Robotaxi Rides. Here’s What It Can And Can’t Do
The gold-colored two-seaters went live in Austin, Texas, after a launch event that had a notable absentee: Elon Musk.
- The Tesla Cybercab, a two-seat EV without pedals and a steering wheel, is now offering robotaxi rides in Austin, Texas.
- The introduction follows a closed-door event where traditional media was not invited.
- Elon Musk, Tesla’s CEO and one of the biggest believers in vision-only self-driving cars, did not attend the launch.
After a hyped-up but rather underwhelming launch event on Thursday night, Tesla’s golden, two-seat Cybercabs are finally offering driverless rides in Austin, Texas. A closed-door party attended mainly attended by Tesla enthusiasts and content creators—but apparently not Elon Musk—marked the occasion and was where a hand-picked group got the first rides.
Launching a car without a steering wheel or pedals is the clearest embodiment yet of Musk's bet that cameras and powerful AI can handle the monstrously difficult task of autonomously piloting a car safely. In addition to the driverless Model Ys that have been available through Tesla's fledgling Robotaxi service, members of the public will be able to hail a Cybercab starting at 5 pm Central Time on Friday, Tesla said in an X post.
It's no doubt a milestone for the company and its CEO, who has promised to deliver self-driving cars on a massive scale for years. Just how big or lasting a milestone this turns out to be will depend on how well the Cybercabs actually function, and how quickly Tesla is able to roll them out within Texas and in new cities. Musk is already behind schedule; he said that by the end of 2025 Tesla's Robotaxi service would serve half the U.S. population.
The Cybercab fleet is small right now. Tesla didn’t say how many Cybercabs are available for public rides, but recently published data from the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles shows that the company has just 45 Cybercabs registered in the state. It's not clear whether all of those are participating in the service or not. What’s more, the two-seat EVs are only available in Austin for now. In total, Tesla operates approximately 220 driverless taxis across six cities, according to the crowdsourced Robotaxi Tracker website. By comparison, Waymo, the biggest robotaxi operator in the U.S., has roughly 4,000 vehicles offering rides in 14 cities.
Tesla left some big questions unanswered about its Cybercab plans—like when the public will actually be able to buy one for $30,000 as Musk previously promised. But we do know more about the vehicle and how it will operate than before.
First off, Tesla bans children under the age of 13 from riding in a Cybercab. According to a newly published page on Tesla’s website, the two-door driverless taxi can only carry adults and minors aged 13-17 if they’re accompanied by an adult. What’s more, riders are only allowed to request a Robotaxi for themselves, which means kids who are out partying can’t ask their parents to hail a Cybercab for them.
The Cybercab also doesn’t have ISOFIX or LATCH anchors for child seats, but the official documentation shows that one child seat can be mounted using the car’s seat belt. This is irrelevant for robotaxi rides, seeing how kids younger than 13 can’t use Cybercabs at all, but the feature may have been integrated as a future-proofing method for when the steering-wheel-less EV will be sold to the public.
As a reminder, children as young as eight years old can ride in a Model Y robotaxi if they’re accompanied by an adult.
Size-wise, the new Cybercab can accommodate two people and has a rear trunk cargo volume of 20.2 cubic feet, which is enough for two checked bags and two carry-ons, according to the company. The trunk, which has a weight limit of 220 pounds (100 kilograms), is also adequate for one large folded stroller and one folded wheelchair. “80% of robotaxi rides are with two passengers; that’s why the Cybercab only has two seats,” one of the company officials said during last night’s presentation.
The trunk can be opened from the smartphone app, and the doors automatically open when the rider is nearby. Alternatively, the doors can be opened via the app. When inside, the doors can be opened from the central touchscreen or from the dedicated buttons on each door card.
The two backrests can be controlled independently, but the seat base moves forward and backward as one piece. Tesla said that the rider’s preferences will be automatically set to the vehicle when it arrives, based on settings from previous rides. These include the interior temperature and all of the accounts for streaming services. When the ride ends, the settings are wiped from the car. There’s also Grok integration, enabling riders to ask questions and get naturally sounding answers from the artificial intelligence assistant.
Inside, the Cybercab has a cabin-facing camera and a cabin radar. The camera checks the vehicle for cleanliness and lost items between rides, while the radar scans for occupants to determine how to deploy the airbags. There are front airbags, knee airbags, seat-mounted side airbags, inner seat-mounted airbags, and curtain airbags. USB-C charging ports are also available.
The two-door EV relies on cameras exclusively for driverless navigation, with a total of eight exterior cameras doing the heavy lifting: one at the front, one at the rear, one in each door pillar, two at the top of the windshield, and one in each front fender.
When it comes to pure specifications, the Cybercab is the lightest, most efficient car Tesla has ever made, with a coefficient of drag of under 0.2, according to Eric Earley, the vehicle’s lead engineer. Documents filed with the Environmental Protection Agency show that the entry-level EV is powered by a front-mounted electric motor that makes 219 horsepower. A 48-kilowatt-hour battery pack provides the energy. The car’s curb weight is just 3,113 pounds, making it about 700 pounds lighter than the lightest Model 3 available right now.
The Cybercab doesn’t have conventional hydraulic brakes, and instead uses electric actuators for the calipers. The exterior of the Cybercab is unpainted. The color is embedded into the material when it’s molded in the factory, which reduces cost and complexity, as there’s no need for a separate paint booth.
And this speaks to the key advantage of the Cybercab, as described by Tesla and its supporters. Since the cab is purpose-built and made by Tesla, it can be a cheaper and more scalable than, say, Waymo's Jaguars or Zeekrs. At a large scale, maybe that's true. But Tesla has a lot to prove before it can get there.

title: Electric Cars Were The UK's Best-Selling Powertrain Last Month
content:
Electric Cars Were The UK's Best-Selling Powertrain Last Month
At 30% of the entire UK market, the country is buying more EVs than any other vehicle type.
- EVs now make up 30% of all UK sales, beating combustion, plug-in hybrid, and hybrid models.
- Tesla is the top-selling EV brand, capturing 8.8% of the UK market so far this year. Kia and BYD are in second and third place, respectively.
- Government policies, plus rising oil prices, are driving the sales growth.
While tariffs and the destruction of plug-in vehicle subsidies have gutted the market for electric vehicles in the U.S., elsewhere in the world the numbers continue to surge.
In the UK in August, sales of battery-electric cars surged 30% year over year, according to data from New Automotive, a research firm. As a result, EV market share hit 30% of new car sales, beating gas vehicles, hybrids, plug-in hybrids, and diesel models. Notably, non-hybrid combustion models only made up 27% of the UK market, so even if they’re not buying a full EV, buyers are opting for something that is electrified in some fashion.
UK EV sales have been on the upswing this year. Data from New Automotive, shows that in July, the country's EV registrations jumped 50% compared to the year before, bringing their market share to 27%.
Jaecoo E5
It’s a no-brainer as to why the UK is EV crazy. For starters, there’s a zero-emission vehicle mandate that aims to phase out combustion engines entirely by 2035. This goal is tiered, with EVs to account for 33% of new car sales in 2026, 80% in 2030, and 100% by 2035. Manufacturers that sell enough EVs to hit the ZEV target get credits, while those who don’t meet it must pay penalties. This incentivizes automakers to develop and sell EV models. The UK also has direct subsidies for buyers of EVs.
The UK also has a lot of Clean Air Zones that disincentivize cars that pollute too much, making drivers who wish to drive into certain areas pay a fee. Cars that are clean-air compliant, such as an EV, don’t need to pay any clean-air fees.
Those incentives seem to be working. Rising fuel prices due to the Iran war have been boosting EV sales across Europe too.
Tesla remains the UK’s most popular EV maker, with 8.8% of the EV market so far this year. Kia is in second place, with 45% of its new car sales being fully electric last month. The UK has also become an important market for Chinese brands. BYD is in third place with about 6.3% of the UK EV market, according to New AutoMotive. Its registrations are up about 60% so far this year. Cars like the BYD Dolphin Surf, Atto 2, and Jaecoo E5 no doubt help with these numbers.
Some of the UK’s own brands aren’t actually helping much. Tata, which encompasses Jaguar and Land Rover, has sold 43,000 units this year, but none of them have been EVs. Perhaps this figure will change when cars like the new Range Rover Electric and Jaguar Type 01 go on sale.

title: Slate Deliveries Could Start As Soon As December: Report
content:
Not all customers who preordered trucks will get them in December, but a select few might.
Photo by:
Tim Levin/InsideEVs
6:16pm ET
Slate customer deliveries could start as early as December,
Business Insider
reported on Thursday.
The company previously said sales would begin by the end of 2026.
The Slate will start at $26,400, including destination fees.
It's unusual to see an upstart automaker move its initial delivery date up, rather than delay it. Getting a car company off the ground is no small feat, and ramping up large-scale manufacturing manufacturing is ripe ground for logistical hurdles.
isn't the only car company that's had its launch timeline slip for a new EV in recent memory.
However, in an email viewed by
Business Insider
Auto told some preorder customers that they could move their delivery date up to December 2026. The most the EV startup has said about its delivery timeline is that sales would start toward the end of this year. Now we have a firm month.
There were two types of early customers; those who put down a refundable $50 deposit just to hold a delivery slot, and those who dropped $300 for a non-refundable preorder. The email was sent to the latter, and it reportedly asked them if they would like an earlier delivery window than initially anticipated. According to
Business Insider,
presented interested customers with a dropdown box for their new delivery window and the earliest was December of this year.
Photo by: Jens Meiners
For customers who want to wait longer, there were reportedly other delivery windows in 2027, including specific ones like "July-September 2027" or ambiguous ones like "coming soon 2027."
When Slate first announced that $50 deposits were open, it received over 100,000 of them. Slate opened up $300 preorders back in June, when it announced the truck's price at long last, and claims it got 10,000 preorders within the first few hours. How many of those people will get a December delivery date is still unknown.
As things stand right now, the Slate—basic as it might be—will be the cheapest electric vehicle in America when it launches, undercutting the Nissan Leaf and Chevy Bolt. It will start
at $26,400
, including destination fees but excluding the many accessories that can drive up the little truck's price.
Going into the end of this year and beyond, all eyes will be on whether Slate can ramp up production quickly and smoothly—and how exactly its unusual truck will resonate in the marketplace. The competition for the Jeff Bezos-backed startup is heating up too. Preorders for the roughly
$30,000 Ford Fathom
open up in early 2027. And it's likely going to come with things like power windows and a radio as standard—features the Slate lacks out of the box.
And, as we learned today, Ford is setting expectations high for its electric truck at
100,000 units in the first year
The Wall Street Journal.
Slate says it has the capacity to produce 150,000 trucks annually at its plant in Indiana. How much room will there be in the U.S. EV market for these low-cost electric trucks? In December, we'll start to find out.

title: How Much Range The Tesla Model 3 And Model Y Lose After Almost 100,000 Miles
content:
How Much Range The Tesla Model 3 And Model Y Lose After Almost 100,000 Miles
In a study that tested the battery longevity of half a million EVs, Tesla came in near the bottom of the pack.
- EV batteries don't degrade as much as people once feared, research shows.
- But results after tens of thousands of miles can vary widely across models.
- The Tesla Model 3 was among the weakest performers in a large study of battery aging. The Model Y did better.
Now that EVs have been mainstream for about a decade, we have more real-world data on battery longevity than ever. Thankfully, it turns out that modern EV batteries hold up pretty well, even after years of racking up miles and charging sessions. Some makes and models do better than others, though. One giant study published this week laid out how popular EVs age, and anybody in the market for a used Tesla Model Y or Model 3 should take note.
On Wednesdaly, Aviloo, a battery diagnostics company from Austria, released the results of 500,000 EV battery tests conducted around the world since 2022. It zeroed in on 20 models and laid out the median battery health score for each model at three different mileages: 50,000 kilometers (31,068 miles), 100,000 km (62,137 miles), and 150,000 km (93,205 miles). The battery health score reflects how much of the vehicle's original, usable battery capacity is left.
While the two Teslas weren't the worst performers—those would be the Nissan Leaf, Renault Zoe, and Mini Cooper SE—they were outshone by most of the pack. None of the vehicles in the study fared all that badly. The Leaf had the lowest median state-of-health, at 86.67%, which isn't bad at all after nearly 100,000 miles.
At 150,000 km, the median Tesla Model Y had 90.32% of its usable battery capacity. That's an EPA range reduction in the neighborhood of 30 miles. The Model 3 didn't perform as well, with a median state-of-health of 88.94%. By comparison, the median Hyundai Ioniq 5 had 93.79% of its battery capacity left after that many kilometers, while the Ford Mustang Mach-E came in at 92.53%.
What's also notable is that the Teslas seemed to lose most of their battery capacity in the first 50,000 km. From brand new to that first milestone, the Tesla Model 3 dropped 6%. But then from 50,000-100,000 km, it lost only around 3%, with only another 3% from 100,000-150,000 km. The rate of loss slowed over time, which is line with what other research on battery degradation has shown. So just because a Tesla or other EV lost 10% of its range in the first 100,000 miles, that doesn't mean it'll be down 20% after 200,000.
Just remember that the median doesn't tell the whole story. The range of possible outcomes is important to consider, too, if you're looking to buy a used Tesla. Aviloo shared a spread of results that it says encompasses 99% of vehicles within each model.
At the low end, Model 3s had as little as 80.28% of their battery capacity remaining after 150,000 km. The lowest Model Y SoH was 82.90%. The high end for each model was 94.53% and 94.94%, respectively. This tracks with what we've observed in real-world examples too. We recently saw a 2023 Tesla Model Y that had a 77% state of health after around 110,000 miles. That car saw an exceptionally long daily commute and lived in a hot part of the U.S.
So while a roughly 10% drop in range looks like a good benchmark for around 100,000 miles in a Model Y or Model 3, that's not a guarantee. Cars that were driven hard, charged to 100% constantly, or kept somewhere hot like the American Southwest might be worse off. On the other hand, if you find a model that was treated well and kept in a temperate climate, you could be in for a pleasant surprise.

title: My First Walmart EV Charging Experience Was A Disaster
content:
My First Walmart EV Charging Experience Was A Disaster
The company's public fast-charging station left me baking in the sun for 40 minutes.
There's perhaps no American retailer better positioned to make electric vehicle charging more ubiquitous than Walmart. It has thousands of stores, enormous parking lots, and millions of customers who already shop there. Now it's taking full advantage, rapidly filing parking lots with fast chargers, even as EV sales are sluggish.
The strategy is gathering serious momentum. Walmart added 368 public fast-charging ports to its stores in the second quarter, more than any network in the U.S. apart from Tesla. Recently, it opened up its 100th owned-and-operated fast-charging station, expanding its footprint to 20 states.
So I went to one in New Jersey to see what it’s actually like to plug in with one of the charging industry's hottest up-and-coming players. The plan was simple: drive my Toyota bZ Woodland press car to Walmart, run our usual 10-80% charging test, hit the grocery store, and grab a snack and an energy drink to savor on the drive back home to Brooklyn.
Here’s what actually happened: I spent 40 minutes at the Walmart charging station, didn’t add a single electron to the press car, and didn’t end up buying groceries because, well, the poor charging experience just killed the mood.
Testing New EV Chargers In The New York Area
I set my sights on a Supercenter in Freehold Township, New Jersey, which had the nearest Walmart charger to my abode in Brooklyn. To be clear, I didn’t need to drive all the way to a Walmart just to charge. I could have simply charged at my neighborhood Tesla Supercharger, which is reliable and easy to use.
But testing the different EV charging providers popping up across the tri-state area, learning how they work (or don’t) and documenting the experience for you, the readers, is part of the job. I enjoy doing it. So I didn’t mind the roughly hour long, 45-mile drive to Central Jersey from Brooklyn to try Walmart’s chargers for the first time.
I drained the bZ Woodland’s battery down to 12% on the drive out and was looking forward to testing how the Toyota wagon fared at this new station. Except this turned out to be less of a car review and more of a charging disaster.
The charging station was located in a huge parking lot, with four Alpitronic HYC400 units painted in Walmart’s signature blue. The hardware can deliver up to 400 kilowatts and serve eight charging stalls, split evenly between NACS and CCS connectors.
The bZ Woodland has a Tesla-style NACS port, so I was relieved that I didn’t have to deal with an adapter. We’re slowly getting past the adapter-hell phase of EV charging as more charging stations with both NACS and CCS ports come online. What the charging industry hasn't fully gotten past yet, however, is the seemingly inescapable smartphone app.
The Smartphone App Horror Story
I knew most Walmart stations didn’t have credit card readers yet, so I planned ahead. Before leaving, I downloaded the Walmart app, created an account, and added my credit card information so I could activate the charging session as soon as I arrived at the station. But activating a Walmart charger through its app was nothing like the experience at Tesla or, frankly, most other major charging networks.
The screen on the side of the charger first asks you to plug in your car and then scan a QR code using the Walmart app. You then have to confirm the number of the charging port on your phone and hit a button to start the session. Simple enough, right? Not quite.
The app’s QR-code scanner initially failed to detect the code displayed on the charger. I tried multiple times, closing and reopening the app and cleaning my camera lens in between. Eventually, the app recognized the code and directed me to the payment screen. I could also select the charger manually on the app without scanning the QR code, but that feature wasn't super clear to me and the app was glitchy.
My card details were already saved. But instead of starting the charging session, the app threw up a “something went wrong” message. I unplugged the cable and started the process all over again. This time, it also didn’t help that the metal buttons on the charger felt like touching a hot skillet from sitting under the summer sun all day.
After another round of plugging in, opening the app, and scanning the QR code, I got a different error: “We’re having technical issues, try again in a moment.” I also tried charging with the vehicle off, and then again with it on, because errors in how a car "handshakes" with a charger can happen too. No dice. By this point, I was pretty frustrated.
So I called Walmart’s customer service line. The representative told me the errors were possibly due to connectivity problems or a Walmart app glitch. Admittedly, cellular connectivity wasn’t particularly strong at the site, but I still had three or four bars and an LTE or 5G connection. All of my other apps were working just fine.
He recommended that I uninstall and reinstall the Walmart app, log back into my account, and try scanning the QR code again. Reinstalling an app I had literally downloaded before leaving home seemed ridiculous, but I gave it a shot. It didn’t work. The same errors kept popping up. I tried the adjacent dispenser a couple more times, too, but that made no difference.
Fortunately, I already had a contingency plan in mind. My backup was an Ionna Rechargery at a nearby Wawa gas station just four miles away. So after several failed attempts, zero juice added to the bZ Woodland, and probably a shade or two of extra tan on my skin, I gave up and headed there.
I reached out to Walmart to see if they could investigate the issue. The company didn’t share what exactly went wrong here, but noted that more payment options were on the way.
“We want charging at Walmart to be simple and reliable,” a Walmart spokesperson told me over email. “We continuously work with vehicle manufacturers and technology partners to improve compatibility. Customers may currently pay for charging through the Walmart app, and we continue to explore additional payment options.”
Hitting up Ionna was a totally different experience. I simply tapped my phone on the card reader, plugged in the cable, and the bZ Woodland started charging in less than a minute after I pulled up to the charger. As I waited for the bZ to juice up, I also noticed something else. There were no other EVs charging at the Walmart station while I was there. The Ionna station, meanwhile, was bustling.
I can’t say for sure that Walmart’s charging problems fully explained the difference in traffic. But standing there watching one station sit empty while another nearby one was busy made the contrast hard to ignore. The irony is that both stations use the exact same charging hardware: Alpitronic HYC400s. The difference was how I was allowed to start the session. At Ionna, I could simply tap my card on the reader and start charging. At Walmart, I had to rely on an app that failed repeatedly.
I don't particularly hate charging apps. If you’re driving a non-Tesla EV without Plug & Charge capability, you’re still going to use the Tesla app to activate charging at Superchargers. The Tesla app has never left me high and dry like this, with one notable exception when a widespread AWS outage took much of the internet down last October. It's been great otherwise.
That’s what made the Walmart experience particularly frustrating. It felt like being teleported back to 2023, when getting a public charger to actually send electrons to an EV could sometimes feel like an exercise you didn’t sign up for—downloading apps, ringing up the call center for help, fiddling with payment systems and credit cards. Exactly the kind of experience the industry is trying to leave behind.
I've tested chargers from providers in the Northeast like Revel, EvolveNY, Applegreen Electric, and others. And although I've seen glitches here and there, things generally go fine these days. Some older Electrify America and EVgo stations have had out-of-order towers, but the experience never got this bad. If one charger didn't work, I'd simply use a different stall. Having to completely change charging locations is unacceptable in 2026.
Some good news: Walmart is planning to add swipe- and dip-to-pay terminals to its charging stations, which should give customers a much needed alternative when the app doesn’t work. Although it’s unclear how quickly these upgrades will arrive and whether every single dispenser will be retrofitted with the payment terminals. The company's charging division is also relatively young, so teething issues aren't too surprising.
Walmart has a vast national footprint, and its decision to build out fast charging at that scale could be genuinely game changing for EV drivers, particularly in places where charging infrastructure remains sparse. But building chargers is only half the battle. They also need to be easy to use, or else they're just expensive hardware sitting in a parking lot, bringing little value to the company and even less for the customers they're supposed to serve.
My experience could have been a freak one-off. PlugShare check-ins show many drivers have charged successfully at this same station. But some drivers have also reported failed sessions and a confusing app, echoing what happened to me. Until those card readers show up, I'd rather plug in elsewhere than roll the dice again.

title: Can Xiaomi Take On Porsche On Its Home Turf? It’s About To Try
content:
Eight dealership groups have signed on as part of Xiaomi's entry into Europe, which starts next year.
Photo by:
2:19pm ET
Xiaomi is officially headed to Europe, including Germany, in 2027, the company announced on Thursday.
Eight dealership networks have now signed on.
German luxury brands have been feeling the heat in China. Now that's coming to their backyard.
Xiaomi has spent the last two years proving that a company that builds cell phones can also build your favorite car. The Apple of the East makes EVs that are fast, desirable, and chock-full of tech that makes most American cars feel archaic.
It's passed the test in its home
market, having sold over 700,000 vehicles there to date. Now it's setting its sights on Europe.
On Thursday, the company announced plans to enter European markets, including Germany, in 2027. After bringing the heat to Porsche, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, and Volkswagen within China, the country's automakers are increasingly exporting the fight to European turf. Xiaomi is just the latest disruptor. Based on its popularity in China and
high praise abroad
, it could be a formidable competitor.
Photo by: MIIT
After years of raking in healthy profits in China, European luxury brands have been
struggling to keep up with the country's fast-moving homegrown automakers
. Their sales have dwindled as a result. Only
125 vehicles
were imported into China in July, a figure that's down 99% from its 2023 peak. One example: Porsche's China sales fell 26% last year and have been more than cut in half since 2021. Now the same tech that is winning over Chinese consumers is headed straight for the Germans' backyard.
Xiaomi SU7 Ultra sedan has already been doing battle with Porsche on the Nurburgring
, even dethroning the Taycan Turbo GT. Then there's the
, a curvy crossover with 990 horsepower, which is about 300 more than you get in the highest-performance Porsche Macan EV. Xiaomi hasn't said which model (or models) it plans to sell in Europe.
If pure speed isn't your thing, Xiaomi is also catering to tech-hungry buyers with its "Human x Car x Home" ecosystem, which integrates more than 1,000 different Xiaomi devices with the car. Xiaomi's cars are also aggressively priced in its home market and have a number of premium features baked in that make a pretty convincing value proposition over many of the offerings on the market today wearing a badge from a German luxury brand.
How well Xiaomi manages to do in Germany, and Europe more broadly, may ultimately come down to price and positioning. The SU7 and YU7 could launch as Porsche and BMW rivals for a much better value. But if the brand prices its vehicles too close to cars from already well-respected brands, that could be a tougher sell.
Stay informed with our newsletter every weekday
Xiaomi is just
one of the Chinese brands
making its way to Europe.
Chinese-imported cars made up 14.2% of all EVs sold across the region
during the first half of 2026, meaning that Western automakers across the board are already feeling the pressure.
Some have even
resorted to importing their own made-in-China vehicles
into Europe
as a way to stay competitive
. But as up-market models from Xiaomi and others gain more traction, it could prove to be a tough road ahead for even Germany's most prestigious brands.

title: 天合储能12GWh储能电池项目环评公示
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，8月27日，江苏省盐城市大丰生态环境局发布公示，受理天合储能科技（盐城大丰）有限公司年产12GWh储能电池项目重新报批的环评文件。
文件显示，本次公示并非建设新项目，而是调整既有在建项目。该项目建设实施阶段废气治理工艺、原辅料消耗等发生变动，按法规要求开展环评重新报批手续，项目主体建设进度维持原有节奏不变。
该项目位于盐城市大丰区大丰港经济开发区，项目用地面积约330亩，新增建筑面积约12万平方米，主要构筑物包括电芯化成分容厂房、PACK模组厂房、储能系统集成生产厂房、应急事故池、NMP罐区等。
据悉，该电池项目产品为磷酸铁锂储能电芯，一期规划4GWh电芯产线，整体规划总产能12GWh。项目实施主体为天合储能科技（盐城大丰）有限公司，是天合储能的全资子公司。
此外，在产能分配上，规划12GWh电芯产能中，6GWh电芯直接对外销售，剩余6GWh电芯内部自用，用于PACK模组与储能系统集成出货。
资料显示，大丰基地是天合储能国内三大制造基地之一，其余两大基地布局常州、滁州。该基地项目2025年9月已实现投产，叠加滁州生产基地，天合储能电芯规划总产能将达到25GWh。

title: 鹏程无限/希倍动力等4企加快储能电芯及钠电项目布局
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，多家企业推进储能电芯及钠离子电池等项目建设，其中，鹏程无限48亿元储能电芯项目进入设备安装调试阶段，希倍动力、超钠新能源分别推进钠电项目落地，焕文科技储能集装箱项目落地永仁。
鹏程无限宜宾储能电芯项目进入设备安装调试阶段
9月3日，随着装载6套新能源容量化成工艺设备的工程车驶入厂区，鹏程无限新能源科技有限公司宜宾储能产业园电芯制造基地由项目施工阶段转入设备安装调试阶段。
据介绍，下一步项目将开展设备开箱验收、就位安装、单机调试及整线联动调试，并同步推进技术人员培训、质量体系搭建及供应链配套等工作。
鹏程无限宜宾储能电芯项目总投资48亿元，总产能54GWh，分期建设。其中，一期项目预计于2026年底正式投产，投产后将批量生产587Ah储能电芯。
1.5亿元储能集装箱项目签约落地永仁
9月2日，贵州焕文科技有限公司与永仁县签署储能集装箱项目招商引资协议，项目计划投资1.5亿元。
据介绍，双方将围绕储能集装箱项目开展合作，并进一步推进储能装备制造、新能源项目开发等相关业务。
希倍动力2.5亿元钠电项目落户自贡
8月30日，北京希倍动力科技有限公司与四川自贡高新区签署高性能钠离子电池生产基地项目合作协议，项目正式落户自贡高新区。
该项目计划总投资约2.5亿元，建成达产后预计形成年产0.5GWh高性能钠离子电池产能。
以此项目基础上，希倍动力将根据市场发展节奏稳步推进产能扩张，远期规划产能规模达10GWh。
超钠新能源6GWh钠电项目签约绵竹
据四川绵竹市人民政府官网消息，8月28日，绵竹高新区管委会与湖州超钠新能源科技有限公司签订年产6GWh钠离子电池生产线项目投资协议。
此前，2024年1月28日，超钠新能源计划总投资30亿元，在绵竹建设8万吨级钠离子电池正极材料的生产基地。此次6GWh钠离子电池生产线项目签约，将进一步延伸超钠新能源在绵竹的钠电产业布局，推动业务从正极材料向电芯制造环节拓展。

title: 注册资本最高达10亿！国家能源集团、华电等4企成立新能源公司
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期，多家能源企业加大新能源产业链布局，国家能源集团旗下两家公司相继成立，国轩高科新设新能源销售公司，华电与隆基合资成立新能源公司，中国中煤也在江苏新设新能源企业，相关业务覆盖新能源开发、技术服务、储能及设备销售等多个环节。
国家能源集团旗下两家新公司成立
近期，国家能源集团旗下企业持续推进新能源业务布局，新设公司涉及风电、光伏及储能等领域。
8月31日，国能准源新能源开发（奇台）有限公司正式成立，该公司位于新疆昌吉回族自治州奇台县，注册资本3.5亿元，法定代表人为陆晓东。
公司经营范围包括风力发电技术服务；新兴能源技术研发；余热余压余气利用技术研发；太阳能发电技术服务；储能技术服务等方面。
股权穿透显示，该公司由国能新疆煤制气有限公司全资控股。据悉，国能新疆煤制气有限公司是国家能源集团二级子公司。
8月28日，海南龙源海控新能源有限公司成立，注册资本2亿元，经营范围包含：风力发电技术服务；太阳能发电技术服务；发电技术服务；储能技术服务等。
股权穿透显示，该公司由国家能源集团旗下龙源电力集团股份有限公司以及海南海控能源股份有限公司合资成立。其中，龙源电力出资1.9亿，持股95%，海南海控能源出资1000万元，持股5%。
国轩高科成立新能源销售公司
8月28日，国轩高科（安徽）销售有限公司成立，法定代表人为陈炜，注册资本10亿元，经营范围含新能源汽车生产测试设备销售、新兴能源技术研发、新能源原动设备制造/电池销售、电池零配件销售、光伏设备及元器件销售等。
股权穿透显示，该公司由国轩高科全资子公司合肥国轩高科动力能源有限公司100%持股，为国轩高科全资孙公司。
华电与隆基合资成立新能源公司
8月27日，华电（鄂托克前旗）新能源有限公司成立，注册资本1000万元，公司地址位于内蒙古鄂尔多斯市，法定代表人为王志强。
公司经营范围包含：新兴能源技术研发；节能管理服务；储能技术服务；余热发电关键技术研发；风力发电技术服务等。
股权穿透显示，该公司由华电新能源集团股份有限公司以及西安隆基新能源有限公司合资成立。其中华电出资950万元，占股95%，隆基出资50万元，占股5%。
中国中煤新设新能源公司
8月17日，中煤电力（射阳）新能源有限公司成立，注册资本1000万元，公司地址位于江苏省盐城市，法定代表人为边登鹏。
公司经营范围包含：发电技术服务；风力发电技术服务；太阳能发电技术服务；生物质能技术服务等。
股权穿透显示，该公司由中国中煤子公司中煤电力有限公司全资持股。

title: 三晶电气、宁德时代等6企海外储能订单新动态
content:
集邦光储观察获悉，近期全球储能市场海外项目加速落地。富储科能、三晶电气、三一锂能、中国能建、宁德时代、三星SDI等6企相继披露相关海外订单动态，涉及储能项目投运、签约项目、达成战略合作等。
富储科能泰国储能项目投运
9月2日，富储科能宣布，近日其AIO 261液冷储能柜在泰国某工厂顺利完成安装调试并投入试运行。
据悉，在泰国持续高温下，AIO 261液冷储能柜依然展现出高安全、高能效、高可靠、长寿命的品质，液冷温控精准控温，电池簇温差维持在合理水平，电芯压差控制优异，消防与液冷子系统全程无故障告警，整套系统运行稳定。
三晶电气罗马尼亚光伏储能项目投运
9月1日，三晶电气宣布，罗马尼亚5.22MWh VPP项目投运。
据介绍，三晶电气携手本地合作伙伴，在罗马尼亚打造2.5MW光伏+储能标杆项目，部署20台CM2一体化储能系统，总容量达5.22MWh。该项目既是罗马尼亚首个采用CM2的规模化工业光储项目，也是欧洲同级别在建的三晶电气工商业储能项目中规模最大的一个。
三一锂能供货欧洲175MWh项目
8月31日，三一集团表示，旗下三一锂能将为欧洲罗马尼亚客户175MWh储能系统提供先进交直流整体设备方案，包含储能直流仓、逆变升压一体仓全套核心装备。
此前，三一微电网罗马尼亚多布雷什蒂光储一体化项目顺利开工，成为集团在欧洲首个大型光储并网示范项目。此次罗马尼亚175MWh储能项目落地，代表着三一储能装备在欧洲市场实现从项目示范到百兆瓦级批量供货的跨越。
中国能建签约非洲单体最大光储项目
据能建国际集团消息，8月27日，中国能建国际集团、西南院和建筑集团以联营体形式，签署摩洛哥米德尔特一期光储项目EPC合同。
项目位于摩洛哥米德尔特地区，主要建设约630MW的光伏电站及1300MWh电化学储能系统，工程范围涵盖勘察设计、设备供货、建设安装、调试及相关服务等。建成后，将成为非洲单体规模最大的光储项目。
宁德时代签巴西储能战略合作
8月29日，宁德时代宣布，在2026年南美智慧能源展开幕当天（8月25日），与南美最大电池企业Moura达成战略合作，双方将联手参与巴西矿产能源部主导的储能容量储备拍卖（LRCAP 2026），共同开拓南美巴西储能市场。
根据合作协议，宁德时代将为其提供储能解决方案，Moura则提供本地制造经验与渠道网络。宁德时代表示，当前宁德时代已在巴西储能市场占据45%的份额，标杆项目Registro是巴西输电领域首个公用事业级电池储能系统。
三星SDI将向某储能系统集成商供应电池
近日，据外媒报道，三星SDI将向一家全球知名储能系统集成商供应磷酸铁锂电芯，交易金额预计达数万亿韩元。双方计划于第四季度敲定一份为期三年的主合同，每年供应量为数GWh。
报道还称，该客户为全球最大储能企业，自身不生产电芯，外购电芯组装储能产品，三星SDI将向其供应电芯而非整套系统，两家公司曾于2014年在中国设立合资企业共同开展储能业务，该客户储能产品此前以方形磷酸铁锂电芯为主，货源多来自宁德时代、中创新航、亿纬锂能等电池企业。

title: OpenAI，真的要造人形机器人了 - NE时代
content:
OpenAI，真的要造人形机器人了
◎ OpenAI要造人形机器人，身体和“大脑”一起做。
△ 撰文：董志洋
“我们一定会做人形机器人，也会做其他形态的机器人。”
在2026年9月1日发布的《Sources》播客交流中，OpenAI首席执行官Sam Altman向科技人员Alex Heath给出了这一回答。
继组建机器人团队、招募硬件工程师之后，他明确把人形机器人列入了公司的开发方向。
截至9月3日，OpenAI官网Robotics团队列出21条招聘岗位，涉及执行器设计、固件、传感器和数据采集，也包括原型制造、零部件采购和训练系统工程师。
从这些研发安排看，OpenAI准备把机器人的本体与模型一起做。研究范围已经深入电机、齿轮和传感器，公司也在寻找制造伙伴，为硬件开发配置人员和供应资源。
Altman还谈到了机器人准备承担的工作。
个人机器人是长期设想，近期更重要的是帮助熟练工人建设基础设施。
他把机器人与芯片、供应链放在一起讨论，设想它们共同帮助OpenAI降低数据中心建设成本。
机器人要适应人的环境
Altman选择人形，首先考虑的是机器人要在什么环境中工作。
开门、在电脑上打字、操作设备、清理厨房，是他在交流中举出的几个例子。这些空间和工具大多围绕人的身体设计，采用相近的形态，有助于机器人使用既有设施。
他也希望，人类继续按照自身需求建设这个世界，再让机器人适应它。
因此，人形成为OpenAI准备开发的形态之一；对于数据中心中的机器人，他认为可以采用其他形态。
这种选择把本体设计与实际任务联系起来，需要频繁使用人类工具的工作，可以保留与人相近的活动范围和操作方式；用途较为专门的机器人，则可以围绕设备和作业空间安排结构。
但在Altman看来，形态还不是最关键的部分。
他在谈到数据中心机器人后说：“相比形态，我认为更重要的是，真正研究出能让机器人工作的「大脑」。”
机器人要使用现成工具，模型与硬件就要共同适应操作要求。
模型生成的动作需要由关节和末端执行，接触后获得的信息又会影响下一步控制。手部的抓握范围、关节响应和传感配置，都与机器人能完成的工作有关。
OpenAI已经将硬件与机器学习协同设计列为机器人研发的基础。
5月31日，Altman介绍，由Aditya Ramesh带领的世界模拟研究，在过去一年中发展为OpenAI Robotics，团队正在招募硬件、运营、系统和机器学习人才。
本体与模型同步研发
OpenAI早已研究过机器人的动作学习。
2018年的Dactyl项目让机械手在掌内调整物体姿态，2019年又展示了机械手解魔方。
2024年2月，人形机器人公司Figure AI宣布完成6.75亿美元B轮融资，OpenAI Startup Fund参与投资。
与此同时，Figure与OpenAI签署合作协议，计划结合双方在人工智能及机器人软硬件方面的积累，共同开发面向人形机器人的新一代模型。
同年3月，Figure发布双方合作的演示。面对“给我一些吃的”这一请求，Figure 01递出桌上的苹果，并解释选择它的原因。机器人还能一边交流，一边整理桌面物品。
这套系统有明确分工：OpenAI模型提供视觉理解和语言能力，Figure自己的神经网络负责快速、精细的机器人动作。
但合作没有持续下去。
2025年2月，Figure创始人兼首席执行官Brett Adcock宣布终止双方的合作协议，称公司内部研发的端到端机器人AI取得了突破。
随后，Figure发布自研视觉语言动作模型Helix，将场景理解、语言指令与连续动作控制结合起来，控制范围覆盖手指、手腕、躯干和头部，并展示了两台机器人协作收纳物品的能力。
Adcock后来回顾这段合作时，强调机器人研发需要持续围绕实体硬件开展训练和调试。他还透露，Altman曾致电告知他，OpenAI正在考虑建立自己的内部机器人项目。
Figure从机器人本体出发，扩大自研模型的投入；OpenAI则开始把执行器、传感器和整机开发纳入研发。原本通过合作连接的模型与硬件，两家公司如今都希望在内部共同推进。
在OpenAI目前的硬件招聘中，执行器是一项重点。
OpenAI正在招募工程师开发定制机电执行器，从概念和架构设计开始，完成原型验证与系统集成。电机、传动机构和传感系统都在设计范围内，结构与散热也需要一并考虑。
公司要求工程师综合考虑扭矩密度、响应带宽、效率和反驱性能，以及可靠性与成本。测试工作包括性能验证、耐久性和故障分析，工程师还要与控制、固件和制造团队协作。
这些指标会影响机器人的实际动作，执行器能输出多大的力、是否及时响应指令、连续工作时怎样处理发热，都与动作执行有关。模型制定操作策略时，需要适应机器人能够提供的力量与响应能力。
把执行器纳入自身研发，OpenAI就有机会同时调整硬件和控制方法。
研究人员可以根据任务提出对关节的要求，硬件团队也能把测试结果反馈给算法团队，用于调整动作和训练设置。
此外，招聘分工也已进入部件内部。
电磁设计、齿轮设计和执行器测试分别设有岗位，热仿真、固件和传感器也有对应职位。公司还在招募原型实验室人员及零部件采购人才。
这类分工涉及本体开发中的实际取舍，调整电机或传动结构，会影响关节的尺寸、输出和发热；改变传感与控制设计，则关系到系统如何获知并修正动作。
模型团队参与这些设计，可以把训练需求与硬件条件放在一起处理。
仿真是另一项研发内容。
OpenAI此前的仿真岗位要求涉及物理求解、传感器与渲染，并关注刚体、软体运动和接触过程，目标是缩小虚拟训练环境与真实硬件之间的差异。
对机器人操作而言，仿真既要处理物体外观，也要处理碰撞、摩擦和接触后的运动。训练场景与真实系统之间的差异，会影响训练出的策略在真机上的表现。
自己参与硬件设计，有助于团队把实际关节和传感器的特性纳入仿真。真机测试出现偏差时，研究人员也有条件结合硬件测试结果，判断应当调整模拟环境、控制参数还是训练策略。
真实交互数据则需要专门的采集体系。
在数据采集运营岗位中，OpenAI要求负责人协调作业人员、设备和物料，组织采集工作站的校准与维护，并追踪设备利用率、停机时间和数据质量。
采集后的处理也有明确分工。
分布式数据系统工程师负责数据处理、样本筛选、自动标注和训练数据加载，为多模态训练与评估提供支持，训练系统工程师则处理训练框架、GPU集群等环节的工程问题。
采集工作站的运行情况会影响数据产出，采集质量和后续处理又会影响可用于训练的样本。安排专人管理采集设备、处理数据，有助于研究团队持续获得训练所需的真实交互记录。
制造合作也已进入准备范围，今年1月，OpenAI向美国制造企业发出合作征集，覆盖消费设备、机器人和数据中心。
在机器人部分，公司寻求的制造能力包括执行器等机电模块，以及精密轴承、谐波传动、齿轮箱与电机。
其中，永磁材料和功率电子也在征集范围内。执行器岗位则要求工程师参与供应商评估、原型制作和供应链开发，与制造伙伴协作，将设计推进到适合生产的组件。
研发团队需要与制造伙伴反复沟通，结构设计要考虑加工和装配，测试发现的问题可能要求更改零件。
供应伙伴能否参与这些调整，会影响机器人硬件的迭代速度，也会影响后续复制同一设计的成本。
值得一提的是，另一家模型公司Anthropic也在研究通用模型如何使用机器人。
其Project Fetch与Claude plays robotics实验，让Claude接入已有平台、编写控制程序或调用已有策略。宇树G1人形机器人的相关测试在仿真中进行，Go2四足机器人实验则包括仿真和实体平台。
不难看出，Anthropic这些公开实验的重点，是让模型操作现有硬件；而OpenAI还把定制执行器、原型验证和制造协作纳入自身研发。
两者都在探索机器人智能，OpenAI同时开始处理机器人的身体应该怎样设计和制造。
先服务基础设施建设
在应用安排上，OpenAI把帮助熟练工人建设基础设施列为近期重点。
五月的招募声明明确区分了近期工作与长期的个人机器人设想；这次交流中，Altman也表示，让每个人拥有个人机器人不是最优先的一步。
Altman在谈到算力建设时提出，公司需要通过技术增加AI供应、降低使用成本。他希望更多人能够充分使用AI，而模型能力提升与需求增长，又会推高算力需求。
主持人把扩大算力投入理解为追加更多资本时，Altman纠正了这个说法：他强调的是技术上的改进。随后，主持人举出芯片和机器人，Altman表示，加快供应链运转的能力会很重要。
讨论OpenAI是否会向行业提供算力时，他说，近期公司自身仍需要这些算力。随后，他提出：“人们经常讨论AI模型的递归自我改进，却较少讨论在物理世界中做到这一点的可能性。”
他的设想是，如果机器人项目、芯片项目和供应链投资能够共同推进，OpenAI就可能以更低成本建设数据中心，并获得更好的芯片。
如果机器人能够参与基础设施建设，OpenAI可能同时成为开发者和使用者，这项投入的回报，便有机会体现在它自身的算力建设成本上。

【NE数据】2026年7月DHT、双电控装机量：采埃孚首次上榜
NE时代根据新能源乘用车终端数据统计，2026年7月中国新能源乘用车插混车DHT系统装机量为25万套，同比下降-16.12%。双电控装机量达到24万，同比下降-16.23%。
■ DHT方面，采埃孚首次上榜，其量产的eRE Plus四合一增程驱动系统搭载于零跑旗舰车型D19。通过复用一套电机、电控和传动机构，在保留发电、按需前驱助推和高效脱开能力的同时，减少了第二套电驱系统带来的硬件冗余，相关系统成本降低 30% 以上。赛克科技同比增长超过500%，上汽变速器和智新科技分别增长44.9%和38.9%，主要与新项目集中上量及配套车型放量有关。
■ 双电控方面，整体走势与DHT市场基本一致，不过，在市场总量收缩的背景下，供应商之间的份额变化依然活跃。弗迪动力以39.5%的份额保持绝对领先，星驱科技以12.1%的份额跃居第二，臻驱科技以10.2%的份额位列第三，同比增长2.6%，前三家企业合计份额达到61.8%。另外，伊控动力同比增长94.4%，智新控制增长56.6%，联合电子增幅超过500%。
PS：该数据是NE时代根据国内整车终端销售数据为统计口径整理，不含进出口数据，统计结果可能会与相关零部件企业的实际出货数据存在差异。
鉴于部分企业的业务模式具有独特性，当前的数据统计方式难以全面、精准地反映其业务规模，故而这部分企业的排名未予体现。如有疑问，请扫描文末二维码联系我们。

title: 电池企业走访 | 善思创兴：电池行业测试仪器专业提供商 - NE时代
content:
电池企业走访 | 善思创兴：电池行业测试仪器专业提供商
近期由NE时代与蓝星锂电联合发起的"电池企业走访"走进善思创兴。NE时代、蓝星锂电电池走访团队一行，深入生产一线与研发阵地，实地考察善思创兴的产业化进程，围绕新能源及新材料领域的前沿应用、核心技术研发突破、行业面临的挑战与标准化需求，进行了广泛、深入交流。
深耕测试赛道，筑牢产品根基
调研团一行抵达善思创兴后，首先参观了企业展厅，全面了解公司的成长脉络与战略布局。善思创兴是一家面向新能源与新材料领域提供智慧科研整体解决方案的企业，核心团队拥有20年行业经验，整合人工智能、信息化、大数据、机器人、精密检测、高通量六大核心技术，产品覆盖智慧科研软件、科研机器人、智能硬件、智能测试仪器、自动化实验平台五大类别。
围绕电池研发与制造，善思创兴已构建起覆盖"粉体—极片—电芯"的测试装备矩阵：在极片制造环节，涂覆不均、浸润不足、力学性能不足、极片膨胀过大会分别导致电芯极化、产气鼓包、掉粉开裂与电池失效等共性难题；针对上述难题，公司在极片力学表征、电池膨胀监测、电解液浸润分析等方向布局了相应测试仪器，相关方案已应用于锂电池、钠电池、固态电池等体系的研发与制程质检。
走进研发阵地，见证表征实力
随后，调研团深入善思创兴研发阵地与测试实验室，重点了解极片力学表征装备的技术原理、数据口径及其在产线质检中的应用方式，并与技术人员进行了细致交流。
极片涂层与集流体之间的界面结合强度，直接决定电芯的循环寿命与安全性能。在极片涂布、辊压、分切等制程中，粘结剂分布不均、局部掉粉、涂层开裂等失效难以完全避免。而行业内常规的极片质检，多采用外观检查与180°剥离测试（PEEL），剥离测试只能测得涂层整体的平均剥离力，无法反映粘结剂在涂层厚度方向上的分布，失效往往难以定位到具体层位。
针对上述行业共性难题，技术团队现场演示了面向极片力学表征的薄膜力学断层扫描测试仪。
该设备通过特殊形状的高精密刀具沿涂层厚度方向逐层切入薄膜，实时采集水平方向的推力与垂直方向的下压力，经算法分析获得薄膜内部不同深度处的剪切强度分布，以及薄膜与集流体界面之间的剥离强度。设备规格参数如下：
结合实测案例，技术人员介绍了该设备的量化表征能力：针对石墨负极与集流体界面，设备直接输出剥离强度（N/mm）而非笼统的峰值力——实测石墨负极平均水平力0.55 N、剥离强度0.11 N/mm，该数据可作为来料检验（IQC）与制程管控（IPQC）的量化指标；
对某极片从表面到集流体实施梯度深度测试，在0–14.46 μm深度区间剪切力呈线性变化（表明材质均匀），在14.46–60 μm区间剪切力逐渐下降，结合成分分析可精准定位"粘结剂上浮"缺陷，为搅拌与烘箱干燥工艺优化提供数据支撑。
在实验室，调研团还了解到善思创兴在其他方向的测试仪器布局：支持多通道同步测力与控温的电池膨胀测试仪，用于识别电芯"呼吸效应"等隐性膨胀失效；集压力机、扣式模具、夹持套件于一体的固态电池测试系统，压力量程最大600 MPa，可配套电动压力机；以及粉末电阻测试仪、电解液浸润性分析仪等材料测试装备。
深度座谈，共话行业未来
在随后的座谈会上，善思创兴董事长江燕燕与调研团一行就电池测试仪器行业发展趋势、技术痛点、市场机遇等议题展开了深入交流。
江董事长介绍，电池产业正从产能扩张转向质量与安全竞争，测试表征在研发验证与制程管控中的权重持续上升；公司坚持深耕测试仪器细分赛道，围绕极片力学、电芯安全、固态电池等方向做深做透，以高精度、可量化的检测数据帮助电池企业将失效问题"测得出、查得准"。调研团对善思创兴聚焦细分赛道的定力与产品化能力表示认可，指出测试仪器是电池研发与制程管控的关键基础设施。
座谈中，双方还交流了测试方案在科研机构的落地情况。近年来，善思创兴的测试装备已在多所高校与科研机构实现采购落地，相关应用得到进一步印证。
双方均表示，未来将在电池测试表征与产业化应用方面保持交流，共同推动行业测试标准与方法的完善。

title: 【NE快讯】地平线征程智驾芯片量产突破1500万；重庆青山大功率同轴电驱规模化量产；兴瑞科技与臻驱科技签署战略合作协议 - NE时代
content:
【NE快讯】地平线征程智驾芯片量产突破1500万；重庆青山大功率同轴电驱规模化量产；兴瑞科技与臻驱科技签署战略合作协议
◎重庆青山大功率同轴电驱规模化量产
◎兴瑞科技与臻驱科技签署战略合作协议
地平线征程智驾芯片量产突破1500万
近日，地平线正式宣布征程®智驾芯片量产突破1500万，地平线征程®智驾芯片已累计赋能800万车主，与超40个品牌达成合作，中国前十大车企全部在列。
自2020年开启前装量产以来，地平线征程芯片实现从0到1000万量产用时5年，而从1000万到1500万的跨越，仅用时12个月，年增速达39%。出货量的持续加速，印证地平线规模化量产交付能力的稳步跃升。
截至目前，地平线已累计斩获500款量产车型定点，其中中高阶智能驾驶领域定点接近130款，在手定点总量超2000万套。随着定点项目陆续进入量产周期，充足的车型储备将持续转化为稳定的出货增长动能。
重庆青山大功率同轴电驱规模化量产
近日，重庆青山工业有限责任公司宣布近日全新一代大功率同轴电驱实现规模化量产，目前已搭载阿维塔、岚图等品牌车型上市交付，并获得赛力斯新项目定点。据公开信息，该产品单月需求已突破2万台。
具体来看，重庆青山采用行星排拓扑结构，将电机、减速器及控制器进行深度集成，相比传统平行轴电驱，可进一步压缩Z向空间。同时，通过低粘度油品、高精度镜面磨削，以及可变驱动电阻、脉冲扭矩控制等软硬件手段降低能量损耗。
上述产品源自重庆青山GI-Drive 2.0智能电驱平台。该平台于2025年正式发布，覆盖混动及纯电等应用场景，并向集中式、同轴及分布式驱动延伸。公开资料显示，GI-Drive 2.0平台包含293件国内外发明专利及119项关键核心技术，反映出重庆青山正明显加快从传统变速器供应商向电驱系统供应商转型。
5V版本的MLX90381可提供2µs的输出刷新率，支持超过50,000rpm的旋转速度测量，适用于直流（DC）、无刷直流（BLDC）以及永磁同步电机（PMSM）架构中的高精度转子位置检测。其可编程的灵敏度和滤波器带宽为优化系统性能提供了高灵活性，而I²C通信接口则使生产过程中的器件配置与校准变得更加高效便捷。
兴瑞科技与臻驱科技签署战略合作协议
近日，兴瑞科技发布公告称，近日与臻驱科技（上海）股份有限公司签署《战略合作框架协议》，双方拟围绕新能源汽车电控、机器人及固态变压器等领域展开合作。
根据协议，兴瑞科技拟认购臻驱科技未来首次公开发行的部分股票，并在核心电驱业务配套方面建立优先合作机制。双方还计划联合研发机器人关节结构件、固态变压器相关零部件，并协同探索欧洲市场布局。
从业务基础来看，双方具备一定协同性。兴瑞科技主营精密零组件，汽车电子是其重要业务板块，近年来也在向机器人、AI服务器等新兴领域延伸。臻驱科技则长期聚焦新能源汽车电控，产品覆盖电控、功率模块、功率砖等，并逐步将电力电子技术向机器人、数据中心电源等场景拓展。
此次合作的看点，在于双方关系可能从供应链配套进一步延伸至资本和技术协同。不过，目前签署的仍是框架性协议，机器人、固态变压器等业务尚处于产业拓展阶段，后续能否形成定点项目、量产订单及实际收入仍存在不确定性。

title: 赛科动力发布下一代高安全及全固态电池产业化成果 - NE时代
content:
赛科动力发布下一代高安全及全固态电池产业化成果
9 月 2 日，作为2026世界动力电池大会同期特色活动，欧阳明高院士工作站先进电池安全创新成果发布会在宜宾三江新区隆重举行。大会云集院士专家、宜宾市相关领导，产业链企业代表、在宜高校院所师生、市属国企负责人以及中央、省级、行业媒体共 200 余人。
本次大会由清华大学车辆与运载学院副教授、清华大学电池安全实验室主任冯旭宁主持，中国科学院院士、清华大学教授欧阳明高，宜宾市委常委、市国资委党委书记刘乃贵发表致辞，聚焦固态电池产业化、固态电池关键新材料、大模型端云一体化电池管控等行业核心赛道，多家企业分别发布创新成果。
赛科动力董事长兼总经理朱高龙在此次大会上重磅发布下一代高安全电池及全固态电池产业化成果。依托欧阳明高院士工作站产学研融合创新平台，以系列工程化技术突破，实现固态电池从实验室走向规模化量产，为国内固态电池产业化进程注入硬核动能。
根植清华大学欧阳明高教授团队科研根基，赛科动力立足底层技术逻辑，搭建分层迭代技术路线：以高安全电池夯实当下产业应用，前瞻攻坚硫化物全固态电池布局未来。
成果一：高安全电池
高安全电池围绕材料、界面、配方、电芯四位一体系统性革新，赛科动力筑牢高安全电池技术底座，同步打造超高比能、高倍率、高安全三大产品系列，适配多元场景差异化需求。已实现400Wh/kg超高比能电池的量产交付，360Wh/kg产品循环寿命大于1000次，在-20℃~60℃全温域稳定运行，并且通过针刺测试，这一突破意味着将高镍电池的安全性做到了铁锂水平。
目前高安全电池已得到工程化验证，GWh自动化产线已持续进行生产，建成智能制造、在线检测、数字化追溯核心能力，2027年将完成 3.5GWh二期产线扩建。产品已广泛应用在低空经济、具身智能机器人、高端电摩等新兴赛道，有效提升终端续航表现。
成果二：硫化物全固态电池
硫化物全固态电池是下一代动力电池的核心方向，赛科动力从本征安全、运行安全、结构安全三大维度持续拓宽电池安全边界。借助AI技术加速本征安全材料挖掘，复合硫化物电解质热分解温度提升超过40%，电解质离子导率超过10 mS/cm，保障高倍率离子传输，为高比能全固态电池奠定坚实基础；自研第三代粘结剂技术，打造高韧性电解质膜，解决薄膜生产断裂难题，提升制造良率、降低电芯运行压力；创新搭建力-电-热多物理场耦合模型，实现电芯结构安全由经验判断转向数字化模型决策。
当前公司已完成 400Wh/kg、60Ah大容量电芯连续化试制，电芯顺利通过针刺、210℃热箱等极限测试，循环寿命突破 1000 圈，扎实筑牢硫化物路线产业化技术根基。秉承“开放平台、技术赋能、协同创新”的理念，赛科动力联动全固态电池上下游产业链建设了全国首条全固态电池智能制造中试线，打通材料-电芯-工艺完整验证链路，将于2026年底正式投用。
未来，赛科动力将秉承“全球硫化物全固态电池创领者”的初心，链接产学研各方力量，以持续的技术攻坚，护航新能源产业阔步向前，奔赴零碳发展的壮阔远方。
赛科动力依托四川新能源汽车创新中心有限公司（欧阳明高院士工作站）孵化成立，公司总部位于四川宜宾。是一家集科技创新与产业化应用于一体的创新型科技企业，专注于固态锂离子电池与固态电解质材料研发、生产、销售。
赛科动力以高安全、高性能固态电池为核心，为客户提供卓越的能源解决方案，产品广泛满足低空经济、机器人等领域需求，并向动力、储能等领域提供全面服务。公司以“为中国新能源持续保持世界领先贡献重要力量”为使命，推动固态电池技术产业化进程，致力于成为全球硫化物全固态电池创领者，推动新能源技术革新，助力全球能源转型

9月1日，工业和信息化部公示第一批国家新兴产业发展示范基地创建对象初步名单。
亿航智能设备（广州）有限公司入选
“低空装备”示范企业创建对象
2026年广东省制造业单项冠军企业
，亿航智能接连拿下多项重要荣誉，标志着企业在技术创新、制造实力、产业示范层面获得权威认可。
此次低空装备领域共有9家企业进入公示名单，亿航智能是唯一以载人eVTOL为核心产品的企业，也是唯一来自广东的企业。从科技创新、先进制造到产业应用，亿航智能持续推动无人驾驶航空器创新成果向现实生产力转化，为广东培育低空经济新动能、发展新质生产力增添新的产业实践。
01 国家首批｜广东低空装备领域唯一
国家新兴产业发展示范基地创建工作的示范企业遴选，围绕产品落地、技术攻坚、业态创新、运营管理效能等核心维度开展严苛考评，旨在培育一批新兴产业标杆主体，充分发挥其示范引领、辐射带动产业升级的重要作用。此次跻身国家首批创建对象公示名单，是亿航智能长期深耕低空装备赛道，持续推动科技创新成果产业化落地取得的标志性成果。
国家新兴产业发展示范企业
作为广东低空装备领域唯一入选企业，亿航智能更实现广东低空装备企业跻身国家首批新兴产业示范创建序列的重要突破，直观展现出广东省在低空装备技术创新、先进制造与产业化落地方面深厚的发展根基，将为区域低空经济高质量发展注入强劲动能。
02 创新制造｜两项权威成果再添支撑
国家级示范创建背后，是技术创新与产业能力的持续积累。8月28日，国家知识产权局公布第二十六届中国专利奖授奖决定，亿航智能相关发明专利 “一种地面坡度探测方法、设备及计算机可读存储介质”荣获中国专利优秀奖，核心技术创新再获国家级认可。
荣获“中国专利优秀奖”
与此同时，亿航智能还成功入选广东省工业和信息化厅的2026年广东省制造业单项冠军企业名单。这一名单重点遴选长期深耕特定细分领域、技术创新能力强，生产技术或工艺达到国际国内领先水平，且单项产品市场占有率位居全球或全国前列的企业。亿航智能的入选，代表着官方对公司在低空装备细分赛道制造硬实力、市场竞争力与行业引领地位的高度肯定。
广东省制造业单项冠军企业
03 扎根广东｜向“新”而行
从核心技术自主创新、先进制造能力建设，到国家新兴产业示范创建，亿航智能持续夯实无人驾驶航空器产业化基础，推动创新成果加快转化为现实生产力。面向下一阶段，亿航智能将继续立足广东，坚持科技创新与产业创新深度融合，以更多低空创新成果转化为发展新动能，为广东乃至全国培育壮大低空经济、加快发展新质生产力、推动高质量发展贡献力量。

title: 累计融资额近8亿元！追梦空天科技再获数亿元A+轮融资 - NE时代
content:
累计融资额近8亿元！追梦空天科技再获数亿元A+轮融资
近日，追梦空天科技宣布完成数亿元A+轮融资，创下其成立以来最大单笔融资，也是国内混动eVTOL领域最大单笔融资。至此，追梦空天科技累计融资金额近8亿元。本轮融资由杭实集团及下属杭州低空公司领投，萧山创投基金、财通资本、不惑创投、前海方舟、国投泰康跟投，老股东航投基金连续第四轮跟投，晓池资本连续第三轮超额跟投。本轮募集资金将重点用于货运机型适航取证攻坚、产品量产能力建设、载人机型工程研制、产业链体系完善以及核心技术团队扩充，助力公司在安全合规为先的前提下，加速技术落地与商业化兑现。
低空经济作为新兴支柱产业，行业竞争逻辑已经发生深刻转变，行业发展由早期概念创新、样机试飞，全面转向适航取证、量产交付、场景落地、商业闭环的硬核比拼。资本的持续加注，充分印证资本市场对追梦空天科技混动倾转技术路线、工程化研制能力以及商业化落地路径的高度认可。
研制端，公司采取“先载货后载人”产品策略。载货机型DF600已完成全流程试飞，型号合格证申请获民航局受理，凭借混动方案实现大载重长航程，多轮场景测试有序开展，供应链与量产筹备同步推进。载人机型DF3000已完成混动模式首飞，按计划推进工程研发，朝着适航目标稳步前进。
在商业化与产品交付层面，公司已初步构建起技术自研、订单落地、整机交付的业务闭环，经营兑现能力持续提速。2026年，公司进入整机小批量交付阶段，实现产品从研发试制走向批量交付的关键跨越。与此同时，公司载人机型研制、适航取证、产线建设同步全速推进，形成技术迭代、取证攻坚、量产交付、营收增长四位一体的正向发展节奏，为后续规模化商业运营与低空场景落地奠定坚实基础。
随着低空经济加快迈向规模化、商业化发展阶段，安全与合规也成为行业高质量发展的根本前提。追梦空天科技始终敬畏生命、敬畏规章、敬畏职责，严格遵循相关法律法规、适航规章及监管要求，将安全理念贯穿产品设计研发、试验验证、生产交付及运行应用全过程。未来，公司将依托本次融资，持续加强适航取证、工程研制与量产能力建设，稳步推进DF600试点应用及DF3000载人机型研发，以安全、可靠、合规的产品与技术能力推动商业化落地，助力低空经济安全、有序、高质量发展。
杭实集团：成立于2001年，注册资本60亿元，是一家以工业企业为底层资产，专注产业投资发展的杭州市国有投资集团。自2018年起，杭实集团连续八年入围中国企业500强，2024年-2026年连续三年上榜《财富》世界500强。杭州低空公司为杭实集团下属全资子公司，管理由杭实集团牵头组建的低空经济产业基金，围绕低空制造、低空物流、低空视觉、低空数据四大核心领域开展战略性投资。
萧山创投基金：重点扶持集成电路、生物医药和人工智能等战略性新兴产业领域及新材料、智能汽车、高端装备和物联网等重点产业领域的项目，以及高层次人才领衔的重点项目。主要采取“子基金”、“直接投资”两种模式进行运作，吸引各类高端资源要素集聚萧山。
财通资本：浙江省属上市券商财通证券的全资子公司，坚守“金为实服务”初心，致力于打造一流券商私募子，勇当服务实体经济、推动科技创新的排头兵。
不惑创投：专注以中国研发、中国制造为核心的品牌与渠道全球化出海的早期及成长期创业企业投资，在早期发掘并陪伴了多家细分行业龙头企业，部分已成功上市或进入上市冲刺阶段。
前海方舟：前海方舟资产管理有限公司（简称“前海方舟”）成立于2015年11月12日，总部设在深圳，在北京、上海、郑州、青岛等地设分支机构。前海方舟开创了中国大型商业化母基金先河，是国内综合实力最强的基金管理人之一，是国内管理资金规模最大的商业化母基金管理人，连续多年荣获清科、投中、融中最佳母基金、最佳股权投资机构TOP20等多项行业荣誉。
国投泰康：由央企国家开发投资集团控股、泰康保险与悦达集团联合参股的持牌A类信托公司，股东兼具央企产业资源、头部保险资金与地方国资优势。股权投资是其核心业务板块，聚焦国产替代与新质生产力，深耕各赛道细分龙头。
航投基金：中国民用航空局主导设立的主体多元化的股权投资基金管理机构，已管理近20只基金，累计管理规模超50亿元人民币，聚焦于民航及低空经济全产业链投资，持续为投资企业拓展行业机遇，赋能企业发展。
晓池资本：一家专注于生命科学、硬科技投资为核心的科技风险投资机构，聚焦拥有规模化市场需求和高壁垒技术创新领域，投资和孵化具有持续竞争的生命科学、硬科技企业，目前在管基金规模超20亿元。

title: Flex Pays $4.4B for EPC Power as AI Data Centers Push 800V DC
content:
Flex will acquire EPC Power for $4.4 billion, adding 800V DC, grid-forming, and other power-conversion technologies to its data center infrastructure business, the companies said Friday. The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory approvals and other closing conditions. Flex said EPC Power will join its Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment, which Flex plans to spin off as an independent public company in the first quarter of 2027.
EPC Power develops power-conversion systems for data centers, utility-scale energy storage, and microgrids, including grid-forming technology, digital rectifiers, and DC-DC converters, with a roadmap for
solid-state transformers
. Flex said EPC Power’s platform is designed to connect 800V DC loads more directly to grid voltages and can consolidate functions traditionally provided by UPS systems and AC power distribution. EPC Power said its 800V architecture is designed for
next-generation AI data centers
Related:
SLB’s $4.1B Kelvion Deal Expands AI Data Center Push
800V DC: Raising Rack Power While Cutting Losses
For data center operators, 800V DC could change how power is delivered in high-density AI facilities. Higher voltage allows more power to move at lower current, reducing conductor requirements and electrical losses. It can also reduce some of the conversion equipment between the grid and the rack.
As rack power rises, the electrical systems serving those racks become a larger part of the facility design. EPC Power’s technology targets the power-conversion portion of those systems, rather than the computing equipment itself.
Power Conversion Becomes a Strategic Layer
Neil Osnato, founder of Persistence Analytics Group, said the $4.4 billion purchase signals that power conversion is becoming a more strategic part of AI infrastructure.
“The $4.4 billion price itself is a signal that power conversion is moving from a supporting component to a strategic control point in AI infrastructure,” Osnato said.
He said higher rack and campus power densities make the way electricity is converted between the grid,
on-site generation
, storage, and computing loads more important.
“AI infrastructure is becoming as much a power-systems problem as a compute problem,” Osnato said.
Power Electronics Change the Grid Interface
EPC Power’s technology also targets rapid changes in power demand associated with AI workloads. Its Agile Grid-Forming platform is designed to respond to changes in milliseconds. The company said its systems can integrate energy storage and on-site generation while supporting grid connections and
microgrid applications
Related:
Solid-State Transformers Power Next-Gen AI Data Centers
Osnato said those capabilities can give a facility greater control over how its electrical loads appear to the grid. Power electronics and storage can smooth rapid changes in demand, he said, while converters can help manage the electrical behavior seen at the grid interface. But he cautioned that the capabilities should not be treated as a substitute for addressing the underlying requirements of a large load.
“Load smoothing is not load elimination,” Osnato said.
For utilities evaluating large AI facilities, Osnato said the relevant information goes beyond a site’s stated maximum demand. Utilities should consider ramp characteristics,
power-electronic controls
, storage capability, on-site generation, ride-through behavior, grid-forming and grid-following modes, harmonics, and fault behavior. He added that utilities must verify claimed capabilities during interconnection. “Declared capability is not demonstrated capability,” Osnato said.
For example, if a developer says a large campus can smooth its load, ride through disturbances, or provide grid support, utilities need evidence showing what the capability is, under what conditions it works, how long it lasts, and what changes would require it to be revalidated, he noted.

EPC Scales US Manufacturing to 27-40 GW
The acquisition follows EPC Power’s expansion of its US manufacturing footprint. In July, the company opened a 167,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Fountain Inn, South Carolina. EPC Power said the facility nearly tripled its production capacity, with 27 GW of annual capacity initially and the ability to scale to 40 GW. The facility produces M and MRACK series power inverters for grid, storage, and AI data center applications and is expected to create about 275 jobs.
EPC Power said its annual US manufacturing capacity is expected to exceed 30 GW in 2027.
Deal Sets Up Q1 2027 Spin-Off Plan
Flex said EPC Power is expected to generate about $800 million in revenue during calendar 2026. Flex also said it expects organic revenue growth of about 40% in 2027 and an EBITDA margin of approximately 30%. The acquisition will be financed through a combination of debt and equity.
Goldman Sachs Alternatives and Cleanhill Partners acquired a majority stake in EPC Power in 2022, following an initial investment in 2021.

title: Self-Improving AI Could Drive Innovation but Strain Data Centers
content:
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes AI systems that can design, code, and deploy their successors with minimal human input. If achieved, improvements could compound rapidly as smarter models beget even smarter generations – potentially accelerating beyond human comprehension and, worryingly, control. For data center operators, RSI would reverberate across power, cooling, orchestration, governance, and certification.
What RSI Is and Where It’s Heading
Although RSI is loosely defined, much like artificial general intelligence (AGI), there are signs it’s edging closer to reality. Achieving RSI depends on fast advances in AI-assisted coding, which labs say are already underway. For example, frontier AI model creator Anthropic, in its report titled “
When AI Builds Itself
,” says its Claude model now authors a substantial proportion of
its own codebase
: “As of May 2026, more than 80% of the code we merge into Anthropic’s codebase was authored by Claude. Before Claude Code launched in research preview in February 2025, this number was in the low single digits.” If sustained, this kind of contribution is a step toward systems that can improve themselves.
Related:
The Corrosion Blind Spot in the AI Buildout
On the hardware side, breakthroughs such as
quantum computing
could catalyze step changes in RSI or AGI. “In the recursive AI world, it's basically an optimization problem. What is the best AI? What is the best AI model neural network going forward? Quantum can support this,” said Jay Guilmart, lead product manager at Q-CTRL. “There's an algorithm called [Grover’s algorithm], which is really good at searching large parameter spaces. It can support the recursive operation to help [the system] perform better and pick the best option faster.”
If AI can repeatedly build better versions of itself, the implications for physical infrastructure are immediate. What does that mean for IT hardware lifecycles, energy use, workload orchestration, and the way we design and operate data centers?
“The basic premise of ‘self-improving systems’ is not new in and of itself,” said John O’Brien, senior analyst at Uptime Institute. “What’s different now is that … advances in AI models and infrastructure
make it likely we are at the point where some of this blue-sky theorizing is becoming technically feasible – or soon will be.”
A practical lens on RSI separates systems that truly author and deploy new code (RSI) from those that self-optimize continuously without rewriting themselves. The latter is already emerging in data centers, often underpinned by reinforcement learning (RL). “Successful AI applications in the data center today often make use of reinforcement learning (RL), a well-proven machine learning technique that uses penalties and rewards based on feedback from the environment,” O’Brien said. “This can work well in closed-loop systems where parameters are defined, such as data center cooling, IT, and power.”
Related:
How AI Is Changing Construction from Blueprint to Build
Systems that can self-improve in situ are already emerging. “Startups Emerald AI and Phaidra are making breakthroughs in early pilots and demonstrators that show the potential of dynamic, self-improving systems,” O’Brien added.
Autonomous improvements, especially in
energy use
, are a goal of a new wave of data center management software platforms, agreed 451 Research senior analyst Zoe Roth. “Players like Phaidra, etalytics, and Vigilent are already proving that closed-loop AI can continuously optimize physical facility variables on the fly,” Roth said. “Current AI engines like Phaidra act as autonomous control layers over existing cooling (Building Management System) and power (Electric Power Management Systems) systems. They don't rewrite their own code, but they do retrain and update neural networks on real-time sensor telemetry.”
Operational Impacts for Data Centers
For operators, self-optimization promises tangible benefits in monitoring and maintenance. “Condition-based maintenance today needs a substantial historical dataset before it can identify fault risk with any confidence,” said Alex Cordovil, research director at Dell’Oro. “A system that improves on its own operating experience could get there much faster and much more effectively, with real gains in uptime and performance.”
Related:
Meeting AI Demand: Alternate Power, Design, and Site Strategy
But that raises a thorny question: how do you certify software that keeps changing? “If a software suite, or an AI agent, were judged capable of performing data center management duties, I'm not sure how you certify something that keeps changing underneath you,” Cordovil said. “You can't certify a moving target.” In practice, this could require ongoing re-approval of models or continuous monitoring and rollback controls that keep humans in the loop, reducing some of the efficiency gains.
“You can't certify a moving target.” – Alex Cordovil, research director, Dell’Oro
Self-improving AI that shifts between training and inference could also exacerbate the wide power swings already challenging AI data centers. “Sustained synchronous training behaves nothing like inference: large fleets swing between near-idle and near-peak in lockstep, tens to hundreds of megawatts at fractions of a hertz,” Cordovil said. “A fleet that trains and serves at the same time would make that a permanent design requirement rather than a training-cluster problem.”
Strategic Outlook and Industry Effects
Beyond near-term design choices, RSI could alter industrial dynamics. A system that can code and design its successor would have huge ramifications for those designing, building, and manufacturing data center infrastructure,” O’Brien said. “Would they want to automate half of their workforce? What would that do to their business?”
For now, RSI remains a nascent concept. But if it’s ever achieved, the effects – good and bad – will extend well beyond the models themselves, reshaping the entire AI stack and rippling through society. One plausible scenario features AI not only coding more powerful successors but also designing and even prefabricating the data centers that will house them. Even then, self-optimizing, self-replicating AI data centers would face hurdles in regulation, certification, safety assurance, and
public acceptance
. Expansion already feels too fast for many communities; RSI could accelerate the pace further.

title: The Corrosion Blind Spot in the AI Buildout
content:
The global race to build artificial intelligence infrastructure represents one of the largest capital investment cycles in modern history. Technology companies are investing unprecedented sums in AI infrastructure and new data centers as demand for advanced computing capacity continues to accelerate. Every hyperscale campus represents an enormous investment in computing hardware, electrical infrastructure, cooling systems, and supporting utilities.
Despite this unprecedented growth, one important aspect of asset reliability often receives little attention during project planning: corrosion.
Much of the industry's attention has understandably focused on power availability,
liquid cooling
, rack density, and deployment speed. These are critical challenges, but they have also shifted attention away from another factor that directly affects long-term reliability. Corrosion rarely creates immediate problems during construction, making it easy to overlook until equipment is commissioned or placed into service.
Related:
Meeting AI Demand: Alternate Power, Design, and Site Strategy
Corrosion is still widely treated as a maintenance issue. In reality, it often begins months before a facility becomes operational as equipment moves through manufacturing, transportation, storage, and construction. For facilities expected to operate continuously while supporting billions of dollars in computing infrastructure, preservation decisions made during these early phases can have lasting consequences for reliability and asset life.
A Growing Challenge for Next-Generation Data Centers
Industry studies estimate that the cost of corrosion is approximately 3.4% of global GDP each year, much of it preventable through established corrosion management and preservation practices. While data centers have historically faced relatively limited exposure to corrosion, the rapid adoption of liquid cooling is changing that equation.
High-density AI infrastructure introduces extensive liquid-cooled equipment, cooling distribution systems, heat exchangers, pumps, valves, and piping networks that combine multiple metals and increasingly complex
water chemistry
. As a result, corrosion can reduce cooling efficiency, delay commissioning, shorten equipment life, and affect the reliability of mission-critical computing infrastructure.
Corrosion Is Often a Governance Issue, Not a Technology Issue
Most large construction projects include well-defined governance processes for quality assurance, commissioning, safety, and risk management. Preservation, however, is often absent from those same governance frameworks. As equipment moves through manufacturing, transportation, storage, installation, and commissioning, responsibility shifts between manufacturers, logistics providers, contractors, and owners.
Related:
OpenAI’s Proposed IPO: A Trifecta of Opportunities, But Don’t Lock In Yet
As schedules shift and equipment remains idle longer than originally planned, preservation activities may become inconsistent or overlooked altogether. Without clearly defined ownership as equipment moves between manufacturers, logistics providers, contractors, and owners, corrosion can begin long before it becomes visible. By the time it is discovered, the opportunity to prevent it has often passed.
Other Asset-Intensive Industries Recognized This Challenge Decades Ago
Oil and gas, petrochemical, power generation, marine, and heavy industrial manufacturers routinely establish preservation requirements before purchasing equipment. Preservation activities are documented throughout construction, verified during commissioning, and incorporated into project quality programs because maintaining equipment condition is recognized as part of protecting the overall capital investment.
AI infrastructure is reaching a similar level of complexity and capital intensity, making many of these established practices increasingly relevant.
Related:
How Changing AI Workloads Are Redefining Data Center Design
Preservation Begins During Design
The most effective preservation strategy starts long before construction begins.
During project planning, designers can evaluate material compatibility, identify potential risks of galvanic corrosion, specify coolant chemistry, minimize stagnant flow areas, and establish preservation requirements for equipment that may remain in storage for extended periods.
Early planning also allows preservation requirements to be incorporated into procurement documents and construction specifications. When preservation expectations are documented from the outset, contractors, suppliers, and commissioning teams have a common standard to follow rather than making decisions independently as project schedules evolve.
Organizations may choose to develop internal preservation standards, incorporate requirements into engineering specifications, or engage independent specialists to help establish procedures and verify asset condition throughout construction. Regardless of the approach, clearly defined responsibilities and documented inspection points improve consistency while reducing project risk.
Preservation Across the Project Lifecycle
Preservation should extend across manufacturing, transportation, storage, commissioning, and operations. Equipment often spends months moving between suppliers, ports, laydown yards, warehouses, and partially completed facilities before entering service, creating repeated opportunities for corrosion. Whether protecting cooling systems, electrical infrastructure, computing equipment, or spare assets, the objective remains the same: maintaining equipment condition until reliable operation begins.
(Image: ZERUST Integrity Solutions)
Looking Beyond Maintenance
As AI data centers continue to
scale up in power density
and capital investment, preservation should be viewed as part of overall asset management rather than simply another maintenance activity.
The question is no longer whether corrosion will occur but whether preservation has been considered early enough to prevent it. Organizations that incorporate preservation planning into design, procurement, construction, and commissioning will be better positioned to protect capital investments and support the long-term reliability expected from modern AI infrastructure.
